At the core of QNB Egypt’s oversight 
system is the Third-Party Supplier Code 
of Conduct (TPSCC). This framework 
sets clear expectations for both current 
and prospective suppliers, emphasizing 
zero tolerance for unethical conduct and 
requiring full compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, 
and policies. As of 2024, adherence to the TPSCC has 
become a binding contractual obligation for all suppliers upon 
the initiation of a contract or purchase order.
The TPSCC outlines a comprehensive set of minimum 
standards that suppliers must uphold, including:
• Anti-bribery and anti-corruption measures
• Conflict of interest declaration by QNB Egypt staff
• Money laundering and sanctions prevention
• Respect for human rights, including non-discrimination and 
fair treatment
• Prohibition of child labor and forced labor
• Ethical recruitment and freely chosen employment
• Fulfillment of labor rights and fair working conditions (e.g. 
minimum wage, workplace safety, grievance mechanisms)
• Environmental responsibility, including the consideration of 
climate change impacts
• Full compliance with applicable laws and regulations
Supporting this framework is QNB Egypt’s Third-Party Risk 
Management (TPRM) model, which is a three-stage, risk-
oriented assessment process:

Supporting this framework is QNB Egypt’s Third-Party Risk 
Management (TPRM) model, which is a three-stage, risk-
oriented assessment process:
1. High-Level Review: An initial screening to identify existing 
risks and determine whether further scrutiny is required.
2. Quantification: Evaluation of the inherent risk exposure 
associated with the engagement.
3. Controls Assessment: For higher-risk engagements, a 
detailed assessment is conducted—typically involving a 
third-party audit—followed by internal review and approval.
This multi-tiered methodology enables the Bank to 
systematically identify, monitor, and mitigate third-party risks. 
It ensures that appropriate controls are in place and allows the 
Bank to prioritize resources where risk exposure is greatest.
Supplier Lifecycle Management and Performance 
Oversight
We manage third-party and supplier relationships through 
a rigorous lifecycle approach encompassing selection, 
evaluation, and termination phases. Each phase is supported 
by clear processes, defined roles, and performance indicators 
to ensure responsible sourcing and effective oversight. 
Selection Phase:
Potential suppliers are vetted based on technical 
qualifications, geographical coverage, and alignment with 
service requirements. The selection process involves meetings 
with panel members and, when necessary, site visits to assess 
operational standards. Final approvals are made by designated

Evaluation Phase:
Supplier performance is assessed on a quarterly basis 
(for outsourced suppliers only, —or more frequently when 
warranted—by an evaluation panel that includes members 
of the initial selection committee and other relevant 
stakeholders. Performance reviews are data-driven, combining 
qualitative and quantitative metrics, and are informed by 
internal stakeholder feedback. Control samples and periodic 
blacklist checks ensure continuous quality assurance. 
Penalties for SLA breaches are enforced, and a three-week

evaluations maintain a focus on resilience and regulatory due 
diligence.
Termination Phase:
Suppliers that underperform in two consecutive evaluations 
(scoring below 40%) are subject to contract termination. Each 
outsourced service is evaluated individually, allowing for partial 
termination where needed. All contracts include pre-defined 
termination clauses, ensuring sufficient notice and continuity 
of operations. In cases involving fraud or unethical conduct,

6.1 Community Development 
At QNB Egypt, community development is a cornerstone 
of our corporate identity and a direct reflection of our core 
values. Our commitment to CSR goes beyond philanthropy—
it is a strategic and integrated approach that seeks to drive 
meaningful, long-term social and economic progress. In 
2024, QNB Egypt continued to invest in initiatives that uplift 
underprivileged communities and improve the overall quality of 
life across the regions we serve.
Recognizing that the effectiveness of social programs 
depends not only on initial implementation but also on long-
term maintenance, QNB Egypt ensures that all developmental 
efforts are designed with longevity in mind. Regular site visits 
and ongoing coordination with local NGOs play a vital role 
in this process, allowing us to monitor outcomes, address 
challenges proactively, and reinforce the positive impact of our 
interventions.

our business operations with societal well-being. Our policy

Following QNB Group’s sustainability framework, our 
strategy was built on three main pillars: sustainable 
Finance, Sustainable operations, and Beyond banking. 
Through these strategic pillars, we embed environmental, 
social, and governance (ESG) principles into our activities 
and operations. QNB Egypt initiatives and efforts 
align with Egypt’s Vision 2030, Central Bank of Egypt 
(CBE) regulations, Egypt’s National Climate Change 
strategy (NCCS) 2050, as well as the UN Sustainable 
Development Goals SDGs. 
Additionally, QNB Egypt aligns with the UN Global 
Compact (UNGC) and the UN Guiding Principles on 
Business and Human Rights (UNGP). 
QNB Egypt updated its regular impact assessment on 
its lending portfolio covering Corporate, SMEs, and retail 
banking portfolios. Given the huge size of our portfolio 
and the tool limitation of allowing a maximum of 50 
sectors, we successfully managed to cover a significant 
portion of 84.43% of Corporate Banking, approximately 
82% of SME Banking, and 100% of our Retail portfolio.  
Within the retail portfolio, we successfully addressed data 
limitations by segmenting it by gender, age, and income 
level.

in shared values, and driven by a strategic ambition to make a meaningful difference. Inspired 
by the QNB Group’s overarching strategy, we are on a journey to achieve sustainable and 
profitable growth, where success is measured not only in financial returns but in the value we 
create for our customers, communities, and the country we serve. Our value can take various 
forms, whether financial or non-financial, requiring an efficient allocation of resources, energy, 
and talents, which drives us to desirable results.

performance with social and environmental impact. Guided by the QNB Group’s sustainability 
framework, our strategy focuses on three pillars, Sustainable Finance, Sustainable Operations, 
and Beyond Banking, ensuring ESG principles are embedded across all activities to foster a 
more resilient, inclusive, and sustainable future.

2.2 Portfolio Composition 
T o ensure a structured and reliable assessment of QNB Egypt’s responsible banking activities, all financed sectors were organized according to the International Standard Industrial Classification 
(ISIC) at the fourth level. Due to the analytical limitations of the UNEP FI tool, the assessment was limited to 50 sectors. Accordingly, we succeed in covering 84.43% of Corporate Banking in 
Egypt and approximately 82% of SME Banking.
These sectors were selected based on:
• Their highest proportion within the lending portfolio
• Their notable Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) relevance
• Their alignment with the national context.

improvement in data availability. This enables us to tailor our products and services based on

high-income clients.  
For the Current and Saving Accounts, youth and females represent 5% and  21% of the 
liabilities’ portfolio, respectively. 
Concerning Credit Products, youth and females represent 5 % and 13 % of the assets’ portfolio, 
respectively. In terms of income level, low-income group represents 32% of the total retail 
portfolio.

Financial Inclusion:
• Understanding Financial Inclusion in Egypt
The Financial Inclusion Datahub recorded a significant rise in the financial inclusion rate 
among citizens aged 15 and above, reaching 74.8% in December 2024, with a 204% 
growth from 2016 to 2024. As of June 2024, 48.1 Mn Egyptians aged 16 and above 
held transactional accounts through banks, Egypt Post, mobile wallets, or prepaid 
cards, out of 67.3 Mn eligible individuals, resulting in an inclusion rate of 71.5%. Women’s 
inclusion stood at 63.4%, with 20.8 Mn out of 32.8 Mn women financially included. 
This progress was achieved through coordinated stakeholder efforts, a supportive 
regulatory framework, various initiatives, tailored financial products, financial literacy 
campaigns, and partnerships with ministries and government entities.
Under CBE’s Financial Inclusion Strategy (2022–2025), the CBE is implementing a 
thorough approach to expand access to financial services for all groups within society. 
This strategy aims to strengthen consumer protection and build confidence in the 
banking system, while also improving financial literacy and enhancing the skills and 
capabilities of individuals, MSMEs, and banking personnel. It also places a strong

capabilities of individuals, MSMEs, and banking personnel. It also places a strong 
emphasis on supporting entrepreneurs and start-ups through non-financial services 
and the development of supportive infrastructure. The CBE is actively working to 
increase financing opportunities for MSMEs and start-ups, helping them transition 
into the formal economy. Digital financial services are a major focus area, with efforts 
directed at increasing their adoption, advancing fintech solutions, and improving digital 
infrastructure. 
In parallel, the CBE is working to broaden access to banking services, encourage 
saving habits, and customize financial products to meet the needs of various customer 
segments. Reducing the 8.2% gender gap in financial access is also a key objective for 
the CBE, with targeted efforts to increase women’s inclusion.
• Financial Inclusion Roadmap
According to our impact analysis and assessment of our retail banking portfolio, we are 
looking forward to setting targets that align with CBE’s objectives to advance financial 
inclusion and support the implementation of CBE’s financial inclusion strategy.

The Bank is committed to ensuring that its services are accessible to all members of the

procedural barriers.

across the country through a wide-reaching network of 235 branches, close to 1,000 ATMs, 
and over 39,000 points of sale terminals (POS). This is supported by a workforce of 7,605 
professionals and around-the-clock customer service.

multilateral financiers, the Bank channels funding to small and medium enterprises SMEs,

Methodology
GHG emissions were estimated using an activity-based method with the following formula:
GHG Emissions (tCO2 e/year)=Activity Data (unit of activity/year)×Emission Factor
Where:
• Activity Data refers to measured or estimated quantities such as fuel consumption (liters), 
electricity use (kWh), business travel distances (km), or waste generated (tons).
• Emission Factors indicate the amount of GHG emitted per unit of activity. For this report, 
EFs were primarily obtained from the Department for Environment Food & Rural Affairs 
(DEFRA) for scopes 1 and 3, supplemented by the International Energy Agency (IEA) 
emission factors for Scope 2 electricity consumption.
• ICAO Carbon Emissions Calculator was used specifically for business travel by air, 
ensuring a standardized and internationally recognized methodology for calculating 
aviation emissions.
Emission factors applied in this report are consistent with internationally recognized

Emission factors applied in this report are consistent with internationally recognized 
sources, including the Department for Environment Food & Rural Affairs (DEFRA), and the

transparency, and accuracy. The assessment was designed to reflect QNB Egypt’s

over time. Where data gaps were identified, reasonable assumptions were applied and 
documented, with the intention of revisiting these in future assessments to strengthen overall 
data quality and reliability.

Data Quality
Evaluating the quality of data is crucial in GHG reporting, adhering to five key reporting 
principles as defined by the GHG Protocol: accuracy, completeness, consistency, 
transparency, and relevance.
• Accuracy ensures that the data is precise enough to reflect the true emissions 
scenario, preventing misguidance in emission reduction strategies.
• Completeness guarantees that all relevant emission sources are accounted for, 
leaving no significant gaps in the data.
• Consistency promotes uniformity in data collection methods and calculations over 
time, enabling meaningful comparisons across different reporting periods.
• Transparency requires that all assumptions and methodologies are openly 
documented, enhancing the credibility of the reported data.
• Relevance ensures that the reported data meets the specific needs of users, aiding 
effective decision-making for emission reduction strategies.

Insights & Conclusion
The 2024 CF assessment for QNB Egypt reported total GHG emissions across Scopes 1, 2, 
and selected Scope 3 categories, covering 3 headquarters and 235 branches. The analysis 
shows that emissions are overwhelmingly driven by purchased electricity, which accounts 
for nearly 94.19% of the total footprint. Direct Scope 1 emissions contributed around 
4.92%, primarily from fuel consumption in company-owned vehicles, while stationary diesel 
generators played only a minor role. Scope 3 emissions represented about 0.90% of the total, 
with Paper Waste and Business Travel as the main contributors.
Activity-based data across all operational boundaries ensured accuracy and transparency in 
the results. This reliability enabled the Bank to establish robust emissions intensity indicators 
of 0.14 tCO₂e per m² and 2.47 tCO₂e per FTE, which serve as valuable benchmarks for tracking 
efficiency and performance over time.

2.1 About QNB Group
Established in 1964 as Qatar’ s premier Qatari-owned commercial bank, the QNB Group boasts 
an ownership structure split between the Qatar Investment Authority (50%) and members of 
the public (50%). The QNB Group has steadily ascended to become Qatar’ s largest bank and 
the foremost financial institution in the Middle East and Africa (MEA) region.
With a vision to lead in the Middle East, Africa, and Southeast Asia, the QNB Group has 
strategically expanded its network, including recent ventures in highly competitive markets 
in Saudi Arabia and India. Operating in over 28 countries across three continents, the 
QNB Group offers a comprehensive suite of advanced products and services through its 
subsidiaries and associate companies.
Employing over 31,000 individuals across 900 locations, the QNB Group maintains its status 
as Qatar’ s highest-rated bank and one of the world’ s top-rated banks according to leading 
credit rating agencies. The QNB Group provides a wide array of investment banking services 
through QNB Capital, which is renowned for its expertise in corporate finance, mergers and 
acquisitions, and project financing. Additionally , the QNB Group offers brokerage services

The Bank serves more than 1.7 million clients with 7,371 banking professionals. The Bank’ s 
vision is to keep all its clients close by offering a wide range of products to meet the diverse 
financial needs of corporate clients, medium and small enterprises, and individuals. T o 
achieve this vision, QNB has expanded its network of branches to 234 branches to cover all 
governorates. Moreover, the Bank continues to enhance its multi-channel automated tools to

how we create value for all our stakeholders. Additionally , QNB has become a signatory to 
the Principles for Responsible Banking (PRB) in July 2022. Our first PRB Progress Report

Since its establishment, QNB has embraced a robust corporate governance framework 
aligned with international standards, fostering sustainable and ethical practices throughout 
its operations. 
The bank is committed to upholding the highest standard of corporate governance, 
prioritizing responsibility , accountability , fairness, and transparency as the foundational 
principles for fostering the trust of shareholder, customers and employees. 
T o this end, QNB has established a dedicated Corporate Governance Department tasked with 
aligning our management practices with international best practices.
In our pursuit of transparency , the Corporate Governance Department diligently ensures the 
comprehensive and timely disclosure of pertinent information and significant developments, 
fostering clarity and trust in our organization. Our corporate governance framework rests 
upon four key pillars:
1. Responsibility
2. Accountability
3. Fairness
4. Transparency .

Structure of the Board of Directors 
The current composition of the board of directors comprises of 11 members, in accordance 
with Statutes of the bank, it is managed by a board of directors composed of a number of not 
less than five members selected by the general assembly from among the shareholders, for a 
period of three years. This does not prejudice the right of the right of the legal person who is a 
member of the board of directors to replace whoever represents him in the board from among 
them.
The Board is structured to include executive and non-executive members (independent 
and non-independent members) to prevent any individual or small group from dominating 
decision-making. Moreover, the Board limits the number of executive members to a maximum 
of two, thereby ensuring that non-executive members constitute the majority .
Our Board of Directors comprises a diverse group of members with the necessary knowledge 
and experience to effectively carry out their responsibilities. They guide the Bank toward 
meeting its objectives while prioritizing the interests of stakeholders. Each member is 
committed to fostering sustainable growth and value creation for the Bank. 
During the election of board members, a cumulative voting system isutilized, granting 
shareholders votes in proportion to their share ownership, thus ensuring proportional 
representation on the Board. The Board of Directors appoints a Chairman, a Vice Chairman,

1. Audit and Compliance Committee
This committee consists of three non-executive Board Members, ensuring that 
the chair of the audit committee does not lead another committee. Charged with 
executing the Bank’ s strategy and overseeing all business activities, the committee 
also reviews issues raised by different Bank divisions and departments. The 
committee is also responsible for reviewing the Bank’ s financial statements and 
ensuring the effectiveness of the internal control environment. It follows up on 
the performance of the Internal Audit and Compliance Departments, as well as the 
mandates of external auditors. Members are required to have expertise in financial, 
accounting, and auditing standards. Meetings are scheduled as needed, convening 
at least four times annually .
2. Risk Committee
The Risk Committee submits reports to the Board. It is tasked with developing and overseeing 
the Bank’ s risk management strategy and determining hedge policies for potential risks. 
Additionally , the committee reviews procedures and the overall risk management framework 
and defines relevant roles and responsibilities throughout the Bank.

3.5 Materiality Assessment 
By assessing our stakeholder and market impacts, we can identify and prioritize relevant 
material topics. QNB employs the double materiality assessment approach, a sustainability 
concept that considers both the financial and non-financial impacts of company activities. 
This approach recognizes that non-financial factors, such as environmental, social, and 
governance impacts, can affect a company’ s long-term financial success. 
In our continuous evaluation of impacts and material topics, we assess and benchmark our 
performance and focus areas against both regional and international peers. This process 
includes conducting a thorough comparative analysis of key material topics and regularly 
reviewing our ESG performance. W e select and prioritize material topics based on their 
significance to stakeholders, their actual and potential impacts, and their severity in relation 
to the economy , the environment, people, and human rights.
Our materiality assessment involves the following three steps.
1. Identify and Assess: Identify topics that may impact our stakeholders and the

Our materiality assessment involves the following three steps.
1. Identify and Assess: Identify topics that may impact our stakeholders and the 
execution of QNB’ s strategy . This includes assessing potential and actual impacts and their 
significance.
QNB considers the material topics identified by the QNB Group. The Bank also considers ESG 
trends and significant topics in the banking sector to gain a comprehensive understanding 
of global sustainability issues and contextual factors that may impact its operations. In 
addition, the Bank factors its strategic priorities, SDGs, Egypt’ s current priorities, national 
strategies, and regulatory requirements into consideration. T o identify QNB’ s actual and 
potential impacts and determine its context-relevant material topics, the Bank has leveraged 
the UNEP-FI PRB Portfolio Impact Analysis T ool (V ersion 3) to conduct its first portfolio 
impact assessment, identifying the most significant positive and negative impacts of its 
financing decisions. In parallel, QNB relies on ESG standards, frameworks, and ratings to 
steer its disclosures and the materiality assessment process. The frameworks include the 
Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB) for 
Commercial Banks.
2. Prioritize: Determine and prioritize the most significant impacts on our stakeholders and 
our ability to promote prosperity and sustainable growth.

For each material topic, we identify the actual and potential impacts—both positive 
and negative—caused directly by QNB’ s operations and value chain on the people, the 
environment, and human rights, known as impact materiality . W e also consider the impact 
on the Bank’ s cash flow , financial performance, and position in the short, medium, and long 
term, known as financial materiality . The Bank applies an internal lens through its risk 
management principles, resulting in a dynamic ongoing process of weighing this information 
to ascertain the importance of various priorities to core business success and external 
stakeholders. The list of material topics in the previous report was modified with different 
rankings based on our priorities. W e also re-defined some material topics and integrated some 
topics together to become more focused and precise. The list of the material topics covers 10 
main topics and reflects our key priorities. 
3. Integrate and Embed: Integrate material topics to drive our sustainability agenda and 
focus areas for the upcoming year and beyond. QNB integrates material topics into its 
strategy and sustainability framework and monitors the Bank’ s performance with a balanced 
scorecard and key performance indicators (KPIs).

4. Sustainable Finance
4.1 Responsible Finance
Environmental and Social Risk Policy (ESRP)
At QNB, we are dedicated to building a sustainable future and being accountable partners 
to all stakeholders. Our ESRP framework reflects this commitment, outlining our approach 
to integrating sustainability into our business practices and managing environmental and 
social (E&S) factors effectively . 
As part of the QNB Group, we align ourselves with its sustainability policy and recognize the 
pivotal role we play in addressing E&S challenges through our financing activities. Central 
to our sustainability framework is the concept of sustainable finance, where we integrate 
ESG criteria into our financing decisions to deliver profit with purpose. Our ambition is to 
assist our clients in managing E&S risks and finance projects that contribute to SDGs and the 
transition to a green economy .
Key Principles
W e are guided by several key principles in our Environmental and Social Risk Policy and our 
internal procedures: Ensuring adherence to all applicable environmental and social laws and 
regulations.
• Upholding human rights, promoting diversity and inclusion, and avoiding involvement in 
activities that infringe upon human rights.

• Acknowledging the direct and indirect impacts of our operations on the environment and

• Promoting sustainable and responsible development through our products, services, and 
financing activities.
• W e adhere to stringent guidelines outlined in our exclusion list, ensuring we do not 
knowingly support ventures that are illegal or likely to cause adverse, irreversible, or 
detrimental effects on the environment and communities.
• W e actively guide, collaborate with, and encourage our clients and stakeholders to 
manage sustainability and E&S risks effectively . By fostering partnerships and sharing 
best practices, we aim to support the transition to a green economy and sustainable 
business practices.
• W e continually invest in building internal capacity and capabilities to manage 
sustainability and E&S agendas, risks, and demands. Through ongoing training and 
development initiatives, we empower our employees to understand and adopt key

objectives.
• Transparency is paramount in our operations. W e uphold a commitment to disclose our 
environmental, social, and sustainability performance in public reporting activities.

The Green Economy Financing Facility (GEFF) is an initiative supported by the EBRD,  
which collaborates with local financial institutions and businesses to promote sustainable 
investments in green technologies. Through GEFF , the EBRD aims to accelerate the adoption 
of environmentally friendly solutions including energy efficiency , renewable energy , and 
resource conservation across sectors. In this regard, QNB is provided with a fund to support 
energy efficiency and small-scale renewable energy investments in Egypt. This collaboration 
provides a one-stop-shop solution for small businesses seeking environmental sustainability , 
where they can access capital loans of up to USD 5 million and free-of-charge technical 
assistance to develop bankable projects. Successful project completion can qualify for a cash-
back grant worth 10%, further incentivizing sustainable investments.
Whether businesses require financing for specific equipment or seek a complete technology 
solution, through GEFF , the Bank offers flexibility through its T echnology Selector and 
Project Assessment services, which simplify the application process and allow businesses to 
focus on their objectives.

The Egyptian Pollution Abatement Programme (EPAP) is an initiative by the Ministry 
of Environment in Egypt that aims to foster sustainable development while addressing 
the adverse effects of industrial pollution on the environment and public health. EPAP 
operates on several fundamental principles and objectives, each designed to contribute 
to environmental sustainability and promote responsible industrial practices. QNB is 
currently participating in the third phase of EPAP (EPAP III), where funding from various 
donor organizations, including the European Investment Bank (EIB), Agence Française 
de Développement (AFD), KFW German Development Bank, and the European Union’ s 
Neighbourhood Investment Facility (EU-NIF), is provided for clients that meet the criteria of 
the program.
The Agriculture Development Program (ADP), facilitated by QNB, offers a structured 
framework for providing financial assistance to eligible clients engaged in the agricultural 
sector. Under this program, QNB collaborates with clients to navigate the eligibility criteria 
and terms outlined in internal documents. QNB ensures competitive interest rates based on 
the tenor of the loan and provides flexible repayment options aligned with the duration of the 
facility .

transactions at various shops and online as well as the ability to withdraw cash from Visa-
accepting ATMs across Egypt. Parents can stay informed about their child’ s spending habits 
through SMS notifications after each card transaction and receive account statements via 
email, ensuring transparency and oversight. With Internet banking access, parents can 
manage their child’ s account securely and perform banking transactions, including charging 
the prepaid card. Moreover, the Automatic Transfers Service (TransClick) allows parents to 
save for their child’ s future effortlessly by automatically transferring funds from their QNB

accessibility . The package offers a free supplementary credit card for loved ones, ensuring their 
financial flexibility and security . For online shopping enthusiasts, the Laky package provides 
a secure platform for transactions with our Internet card and a special 25% discount on card 
issuance fees. It also provides exclusive discounts on the Bank’ s safe boxes for the secure 
storage of cherished items. Furthermore, various credit card offers are available throughout 
the year, providing additional savings and rewards. As part of our commitment to supporting 
working mothers, eligibility for a special discount on the break option, which allows the 
postponement of cash loan instalments for up to three months during maternity leave, is 
provided. With the Laky package, empowerment and support in every aspect of the financial 
journey are ensured, and personalized care and attention are provided for our valued clients.

our branches, Internet Banking, emails, social media, and follow-ups with the concerned

5.1 Financial Resilience
During the reporting period 2022–2023, QNB made significant progress in key financial 
metrics, highlighting its robust performance, financial strength, and the success of our 
strategies and initiatives. These metrics indicate consistent and sustainable growth across 
all major financial indicators. Noteworthy improvements include increased interest income, 
more efficient expense management, expanded asset volumes, higher deposits, improved 
capital ratios, and various other factors detailed in our 2023 financial statements.
The Bank’ s total interest income achieved a growth rate of 4.8%, 30.2%, and 54.7% in 2021, 
2022, and 2023 respectively , reaching EGP 30.88 billion in 2023. This growth corresponds to 
the effective interest rate management and strategic initiatives that have fostered sustained 
revenue growth over the past three years, reflecting our commitment to optimizing our 
financial performance and adapting to market conditions to ensure a strong and resilient 
income stream.
QNB achieved consistent increases in deposits with growth rates of 26.6%, 37.5%, and 30.4% 
in 2021, 2022, and 2023 respectively . This consistent growth reflects our customer-centric 
approach and financial stability . 
The Bank’ s net profit increased by 1.8%, 35.7%, and 56.8% in 2021, 2022, and 2023 
respectively to reach EGP 16.23 billion in 2023. This margin reflects our successful financial

trajectory in the number of full-time employees within the organization. Starting at 6,844

its ability to expand its operations and maintain a steady level of staffing to meet its 
objectives. Such sustained growth in full-time employment suggests a healthy environment.

decrease in 2023 to 2,683, consistent growth in the middle age bracket from 2021 to 2023, with 
employee numbers reaching 3,932 in 2022 and 4,134 in 2023, and a gradual rise in employees

workforce capable of meeting the demands of the Bank.
Turning our attention to employee turnover, the annual rate has seen notable fluctuations 
over the years. In 2021, our turnover rate was 4.50%; this increased to 6.64% in 2022 before 
slightly decreasing to 6.37% in 2023. These figures represent the percentage of employees 
who departed from our company , whether voluntarily or involuntarily , relative to the 
total number of employees in the Bank during the respective year. The total turnover, 
encompassing both voluntary and involuntary departures, also fluctuated over the three-
year period. Starting at 307 employees in 2021, it increased to 471 employees in 2022 before 
slightly decreasing to 460 employees in 2023.

Training and Development
During the reporting period, QNB showed a strong commitment to nurturing talent through 
significant investments in training and development. The Bank’ s diverse programs cover 
technical, banking, and interpersonal skills, ensuring comprehensive developmental 
opportunities tailored to professional needs.
QNB’ s strategies include conducting training needs analyses, encouraging participation in 
international certification programs, and funding postgraduate studies through its Education 
Support Program. New employees benefit from an Induction Program, while international 
and executive leadership programs prepare staff for leadership roles. Specialized training is 
provided via initiatives like the QNB Credit Program and QNB Retail Academy .
The Bank’ s dedication is evident in the increasing training hours, rising from 113,236 in 2021 
to 192,229 in 2023, with average training hours per employee increasing from 16.6 to 26.6. 
QNB also embraces eLearning, adapting to modern methodologies.
Performance reviews are conducted annually for all employees, ensuring gender equity and 
continuous growth. Investment in learning and development rose from EGP 20 million in 
2021 to EGP 29.87 million in 2023. In 2023, training coverage for targeted employees reached

5.3 Responsible Procurement 
QNB implements sustainable procurement practices to ensure all supplier and third-party 
engagements align with our ethical standards and strategic objectives. Our procurement 
strategy is designed to mitigate risks associated with outsourcing and third-party 
relationships and emphasize transparency , accountability , and compliance with local 
and international regulations. At QNB, procurement involves a structured approach to 
selecting, evaluating, and terminating supplier and third-party relationships, with key 
responsibilities distributed across various teams to ensure thorough oversight and effective 
risk management.
During the selection phase, potential companies are proposed and vetted based on technical 
requirements, geographical coverage, and other essential criteria. Then, a thorough process 
is followed to assess the proposed companies, including meetings with selection panel 
members and site visits to the companies’ premises if necessary . Recommendations are 
then presented, and final decisions are made by the appropriate authorities. The selected 
companies must provide a Letter of Guarantee if required, and the Compliance Division must 
approve all outsourcing activities before contracts are signed. The Business Continuity team 
ensures the continuity of outsourcing companies throughout the contractual relationship.

classification: تقرير بنك: بنك قطر الوطني QNB
chunk_text:
[توثيق مرجعي للوكيل الذكي: تقرير بنك: بنك قطر الوطني QNB - المستند: Sustainability+Report+Website22-8-2024.pdf - موضع: 50]
ensures the continuity of outsourcing companies throughout the contractual relationship. 
The selection phase has a Service Level Agreement (SLA) of one month after receiving 
confirmation from the CBE if necessary .
In the evaluation phase, the performance of outsourced companies is reviewed quarterly , or 
more frequently if needed. The evaluation panel, comprising members of the selection panel 
and potentially additional representatives, reviews the performance of the companies and 
takes corrective actions as necessary . Control samples are periodically reviewed for quality 
assurance, and blacklist checks are conducted during contract renewals. The evaluation 
panel gathers feedback through surveys and reviews both qualitative and quantitative 
performance metrics, while the Business Continuity team ensures due diligence for all 
outsourcing activities. Penalties for deviations from the SLA are outlined and enforced, with 
the SLA for the evaluation phase being three weeks.
The termination phase involves meetings with companies that fail to meet the Bank’ s 
requirements; companies that score below 40% in two consecutive evaluations are subject 
to termination. Each service provided by a company is evaluated and terminated separately 
if necessary . All contracts include termination clauses to ensure adequate notice periods.

One of our primary focuses is responsible waste management, particularly concerning the 
disposal of shredded papers. In both 2022 and 2023, we have ensured that our shredded 
papers are disposed of responsibly by sending them to a recycling service provider. This 
commitment to recycling is a crucial aspect of our sustainability efforts as it minimizes the 
environmental impact of our paper waste while also contributing to the circular economy . By 
partnering with recycling service providers, we are able to divert a significant portion of our 
paper waste, reducing our ecological footprint and promoting environmental stewardship in 
the banking industry .
Additionally , one of the key strategies we have employed is increasing our reliance on 
electronic tools, like the workflow tool, to handle operations and document circulation, 
especially for tasks like credit proposals and memos. Moreover, our commitment to sourcing 
paper that is certified by reputable organizations like FSC or PEFC, or composed entirely of 
recycled material, aligns with sustainable practices and further reduces the environmental 
impact of paper consumption. 
There has been a noticeable decrease in the total waste generated by the Bank, measured 
in both tons of CO2eq and kilograms. This decline reflects the effectiveness of our efforts in 
embracing digital solutions and minimizing paper usage.

QNB’ s focus on community development and corporate social responsibility reflects its 
core values and beliefs in promoting social and economic progress. Throughout the year, 
the Bank dedicated significant efforts to uplifting underprivileged groups and enhancing 
the quality of life in the communities it serves. Central to this mission is the importance of 
preserving the results of developmental projects to ensure their long-term effectiveness and 
sustainability . Regular visits and coordination with NGOs are instrumental in achieving this 
goal, guaranteeing that CSR initiatives remain impactful and well-maintained.
CSR Strategy
QNB’ s CSR policy is based on conducting business and CSR activities in an integrated 
and continuous manner to contribute to a sustainable society , simultaneously achieving 
commercial success and QNB’ s long-term strategic vision.
Funding for CSR activities is determined by top management and the BoD, ensuring that 
decisions regarding financial allocations are made at the highest levels of the Bank. Our 
CSR agenda is based on the core pillars of education, health, social development, financial 
capacity development, financial education, and disaster recovery , as well as implementing 
initiatives to support our communities in line with the pillars of corporate social 
responsibility .
CSR Initiatives
QNB’ s CSR initiatives exemplify a diversified approach that has impacts across all governorates

CSR Initiatives
QNB’ s CSR initiatives exemplify a diversified approach that has impacts across all governorates 
in Egypt. Rather than focusing solely on one region, the Bank’ s CSR endeavours are carefully 
crafted to address the diverse needs of communities nationwide. By strategically implementing 
initiatives in various governorates, QNB ensures that its outreach encompasses urban and rural 
areas alike, reaching individuals and families in different socio-economic contexts.
Our CSR initiatives are not only diverse in their geographic reach across governorates but 
also span various fields, ensuring a comprehensive impact. 
A. Medical Care
In 2022, QNB played a crucial role in supporting health facilities across Egypt by addressing 
shortages of medical equipment through donations to hospitals that provide free services. 
These efforts aimed to eliminate waiting lists and deliver high-quality medical services to the 
most vulnerable groups in all of Egypt’ s governorates. Beneficiary institutions included:
• Ashmon General Hospital and Al Shohada Central Hospital in the Menoufia governorate
• Nabaroh Central Hospital in the Dakahlia governorate
• The Orthopedics and Traumatology Department at Kasr Al-Aini, Cairo University Hospital
• The Center of Nephrology and Urology at Mansoura University , the Magdi Y acoub Heart 
Foundation
• The Ibrahim Ahmed Badran Charitable Foundation for Medical Convoys, the Josaab 
Foundation

• Shafa Al-Orman Hospital in the Luxor governorate.
 Additionally , QNB supported the Medical Eyes Convoy initiative in collaboration with 
the Al Orman Association, which provides medical check-ups, treatment, and surgery to 
underprivileged individuals. Furthermore, QNB supported the Medical Convoy for Children, 
which focuses on the Menoufia governorate and operates in partnership with the Ibrahim 
Ahmed Badran Charitable Foundation to ensure young patients receive essential medical 
care and attention.
In 2023, QNB continued its commitment to supporting healthcare by donating essential 
medical devices to hospitals that provide free services. Beneficiary institutions included:

• The Josaab Foundation

Additionally , QNB launched medical convoys for the elderly in the Cairo and Dakahlia 
governorates in cooperation with the Ibrahim Ahmed Badran Charitable Foundation.

B. Social W elfare
In 2022, QNB contributed to various development projects aimed at improving the living 
conditions of poor families. For the fourth consecutive year, the Bank participated in the 
national Hayah Karima initiative, which focuses on enhancing the housing environment 
for the most deserving families in targeted villages. Several projects were implemented, 
including the development of the Hanoot village in Zefta Center in the Gharbia governorate 
and the provision of water connections to 100 homes in the Gharbia and Sharkeya 
governorates in cooperation with the Al Orman Association. The Bank also participated 
in the Winter Campaign in collaboration with the Misr El Kheir Foundation, financing 
the construction of 36 rooftops for houses in the Aswan, Ismailia, Gharbia, and Beni-Suef 
governorates. Additionally , QNB supported the T ahia Misr Fund in developing destitute 
villages and contributed to the development of the Shoprabil village in El Santa Center in 
cooperation with the Al Orman Association.
In 2023, QNB participated in renovating the water network in the Mansheya Abou Amer 
village in Husseiniya Center in the Sharkeya governorate in partnership with the Misr El 
Kheir Foundation.

D. Support for People with Special Needs
In 2022, QNB, in collaboration with the Misr El Kheir Foundation, donated 100 prosthetic 
devices to individuals with special needs residing in the Shatora village, Sohag Governorate, 
and Menyet El Nasr Center, Dakahleya Governorate. Additionally , QNB provided 18 kiosk 
projects for beneficiaries with disabilities in the Menoufia governorate in cooperation with 
the Al Orman Association as part of the state’ s plan to empower and integrate them into 
society under the Decent Life initiative.
In 2023, QNB, in partnership with the Misr El Kheir Foundation, donated 90 prosthetic 
devices to people with special needs in Hayah Karima villages in Assiut Governorate in line 
with the state’ s plan to integrate them into society .

The assurance was conducted by DCarbon’ s multidisciplinary independent team of experts in

The nature, timing, and extent of procedures followed were based on multiple rounds of

was responsible for identifying material sustainability issues, establishing and maintaining

alignment, data mining, and verifications.

•  Review the evidence of internal policies, procedures, and strategy documents provided by 
QNB.
•  Review of materiality and stakeholders’ engagement process deployed by QNB.

can lead to operational, legal, or reputational consequences. Accordingly, the Bank views 
the management of E&S risks as an integral part of its overall Risk Management and  
Governance Framework.

guidelines for sustainable finance, QNB Egypt adopts and operationalises these principles 
within the local context. The Bank’s ESRM Policy Framework establishes the foundation for 
identifying, assessing, and managing E&S risks across its lending, investment and  
operational activities. 
	• QNB Egypt is committed to conducting its business in an environmentally and socially  
responsible manner. This Policy Framework sets QNB Egypt’s minimum standards for  
identifying, assessing, mitigating, and monitoring E&S risks across the credit lifecycle. The 
Policy also lists activities that the Bank does not finance (Exclusion list).

framework Environmental factors focus on issues such as climate change, biodiversity loss,

This Third-Party Supplier Code of Conduct document sets out the expectations, principles, and standards Qatar 
National Bank (S.A.E) requires all existing and prospective Third-Party Suppliers to adhere to.
1. Introduction
Qatar National Bank (S.A.E) (“QNB”) is committed to ethical business practices, sustainability, and high standards 
of integrity throughout our businesses, partnerships, and our supply chain. Responsible sourcing is one our key 
commitments to ensure that we continue to deliver financial services with the highest professional standards within 
the communities we serve. QNB has a zero tolerance policy towards unethical conduct and has developed its Third 
Party Supplier Code of Conduct (“TPSCC”) outlining the minimum standards that third parties (suppliers, contractors, 
vendors, consultants, agents, service providers, providers of materials and products), their parent companies, 
subsidiaries, sub-contractors, associated entities and all personnel (permanent, temporary, contract workers)
employed or engaged to provide services to QNB are expected to adhere to when conducting business with and 
entering into arrangements with QNB.
2.     Scope of Application
Third parties are required to fully comply with all applicable laws, regulations and QNB applicable policies when 
conducting business with QNB, the scope and provisions set out in the QNB TPSCC are minimum standards, 
requirements, expectations, and principles to be adhered to by all third parties.

requirements, expectations, and principles to be adhered to by all third parties.
QNB expects third parties to assist QNB in the fulfillment of any legal and regulatory obligations that may arise in the 
course of the relationship. Third party suppliers are required to read and pledge to commit to the minimum standards 
and requirements of third-party suppliers. In addition, it should be noted that the provisions in this code will be
binding on the supply of a contract or procurement order. The standards of the TPSCC are in addition to and not in 
lieu of provisions of any agreement or contract between third party suppliers and QNB.
  3.   Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption
QNB is committed to the prevention of bribery and corruption through all its business dealings and practices, and it is 
expected that our third-party suppliers will adhere to these standards as well.
It is prohibited to engage any third party who you know or reasonably suspect of engaging in bribery.
Appropriate due diligence should be undertaken before any third parties are engaged.
The appropriate level of due diligence will vary depending on the circumstances and the judgment are made on a case 
by case basis.
Third party suppliers must not engage in any form of corrupt practices, including but not limited to extortion, fraud, 
bribery, and collusion and shall ensure they have appropriate anti-bribery and anti-corruption policies, programs and

Third party suppliers must not engage in offering, paying, soliciting, or receiving (directly or otherwise) any form of 
bribe, which may be considered an illicit inducement or reward for any business transaction such as (but not limited to) 
monetary gifts, loans, commissions, services, pleasure trips and gifts.
4.     Conflict of Interest
All individuals and entities providing goods or services to QNB must maintain the highest ethical standards and avoid 
any situation that may give rise to a conflict between personal interests and the interests of QNB. This would include, 
but is not limited to, situations where personal, financial, or familial interests interfere with fair and impartial business 
decision making. Suppliers shall disclose to QNB in writing any situation, relationship, or circumstance that may 
give rise to a conflict of interest. Failure to disclose a potential conflict of interest may result in the termination of the 
business relationship.
5.      Money Laundering and Sanctions
QNB meets Local and international Anti Money Laundering (AML) and Counter T errorist Financing (CTF) laws and 
regulations, QNB has a zero-tolerance approach to non-compliance with AML, CTF and sanctions requirements.
W e expect our third parties to adhere to these laws and regulations as well.
6.     Human Rights
All third-party suppliers shall comply with all applicable human rights related laws in respect of their employees and

6.     Human Rights
All third-party suppliers shall comply with all applicable human rights related laws in respect of their employees and 
business operations. They should also conduct their business activities in a manner which respects human rights 
as set out in the Egyptian law and the UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the core conventions of the 
International Labor Organization (ILO).
Harassment, harsh or inhumane treatment of employees will not be tolerated. All employees must be treated with 
dignity and respect and suppliers must not use any, threats of violence, sexual exploitation or abuse, verbal or 
psychological harassment or abuse.
7.     Child Labor
All third-party suppliers shall at a minimum ensure adherence and consistent practice with the rights set forth in 
the Egyptian laws and the Convention on the Rights of the Child by the ILO and such other requirements may be 
recognized by   any country where performance in whole or in part of a contract takes place.
8.     Discrimination, Treatment and Equal Opportunities
All third-party suppliers shall ensure that equality of opportunity and treatment in respect of employment and 
occupation without discrimination (e.g. age, gender and ethnic origin) as may be recognized under the Egyptian laws   
or countries where the performance, in whole or in part, of a contract takes place.
T erms and conditions apply

9.      Freely Chosen Employment and Ethical Recruitment
All on -demand suppliers shall demonstrate that employment is voluntary and ensure ethical recruitment practices 
within their businesses and respective supply chains. Suppliers must not engage in or support any form of slavery, 
forced or compulsory, bonded, prison, indentured labor, or human trafficking of involuntary labor through threat, 
force, fraudulent claims, coercion, or duress. Third party suppliers must also not permit their subcontractors to engage 
in these practices. Third party suppliers shall fully comply with the requirements of applicable slavery, forced labor, 
human trafficking, freedom of association and the right to collective bargaining laws of country or countries where the 
performance on whole or in part, of a contract takes place.
10.   Labor Rights and Labor Practices
QNB is committed to promoting fair labor practices and respecting the rights of workers throughout its operations. QNB 
expects its third-party suppliers to comply with all laws and regulations related to labor rights and to implement fair 
labor practices throughout their operations. Suppliers shall pay all workers and employees at least the minimum wage 
as required by applicable laws and regulations and provide all legally mandated benefits in a timely manner. Suppliers 
shall provide workers and employees with reasonable working hours within and not exceeding the maximum allowed

shall provide workers and employees with reasonable working hours within and not exceeding the maximum allowed 
by local labor laws, accommodation in accordance with acceptable living conditions, and proper rest days as may be 
required by applicable laws and regulations.
All employment conditions should be clearly communicated to employees and any wage deductions should be in 
compliance with the applicable domestic laws. W orkers shall be enabled to openly communicate and share grievances 
with management regarding working conditions and management practices without fear of reprisal, intimidation, or 
harassment.
11.   Management, Monitoring and Evaluation
QNB expects that its third-party suppliers have developed appropriate management systems related to the content 
of this code and any arrangements with QNB in order to ensure its objectives and requirements are met, QNB expects 
that third party suppliers actively review, monitor and modify their management processes and operations to ensure 
compliance. QNB may conduct annual on-site visits to evaluate and inspect third party suppliers’ operations, facilities 
and offices, as well as those of their sub-contractors in Egypt. The scope of these visits will be determined by factors 
such as the supplier’ s sector, size, geographical location, and the type of work performed. These visits are conducted to 
review progress, assess risk, and ensure adherence to agreed-upon standards.

Third party suppliers must at all times demonstrate compliance with the QNB TPSCC on request. This includes 
providing any Quality certificate according the nature of suppliers activity upon request. Furthermore, third-party

information including, but not limited to, supplier factory locations, supplier sub-contractor names and locations 
and results of historic audits. Suppliers must ensure that documentation is retained to enable them to meet those 
requirements and demonstrate compliance with the QNB TPSCC.

12.   Health and Safety
Third party suppliers shall ensure that they meet all the legal and regulatory requirements and obligations pertaining 
to health and safety and so far as is reasonably practical to ensure their employees have a safe working environment 
within the country or countries where the performance, in whole or in part, of a contract takes place.
In addition, third-party suppliers must establish and maintain a comprehensive Health and Safety policy that outlines 
their commitment to safety standards and practices. They should be prepared to share this policy upon request as a 
demonstration of their commitment to ensuring the well-being of their employees and compliance with relevant health 
and safety regulations.
13.    Environment and Sustainability
QNB requires all third party suppliers to comply with all legal and regulatory requirements relating to protection 
of the environment. Suppliers should wherever possible support a proactive approach to promote environmentally 
sustainable practices, initiatives, awareness, and responsibility including but not limited to, conservation, recycling, 
environmentally friendly technologies and effective waste management.
On a best effort basis, third party suppliers should reduce operational environmental impacts such as electricity and 
gas consumption, travel emissions, water consumption, management of hazardous materials, and waste and recycling 
production, especially greenhouse emissions.
14.    Climate Change

14.    Climate Change
Climate change and Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions are major global challenges that have significant impacts on the 
environment, human health and economies. QNB expects its third-party suppliers to be aware of the impacts of their 
operations on the environment, including their GHG emissions.
Suppliers are also expected to comply with all relevant laws and regulations related to GHG emissions. In addition, QNB 
encourages its suppliers to consider the use of renewable energy sources and to adopt best practices to reduce their 
environmental footprint.
15.    Information, Data security and Data Privacy
Third party suppliers shall comply with QNB’ s requirements relating to confidentiality, security, data privacy and 
intellectual property protection as set out in the QNB Information Security Policy.
 Suppliers shall ensure that appropriate controls are in place to protect QNB’ s brand, intellectual property against 
unauthorized use and damage. Any information used or disclosed in the business relationship with QNB that is non-
public and proprietary must be protected against loss and infringement. Any disclosure or use of such information must 
only be for the purposes authorized by the contractual agreement. In case of sub-contracting the sharing and disclosure 
of any confidential information is strictly prohibited unless the consent of QNB is granted third party suppliers shall

16.    Cybersecurity
With the increasing reliance on technology and the internet in business operations, cybersecurity is a critical concern 
for QNB. QNB expects its third-party suppliers to take appropriate measures to protect against cyber threats, such as 
implementing robust security controls and compliance with relevant laws, regulations and related standards related to 
cybersecurity.
Suppliers must have a plan in place to identify and mitigate potential cybersecurity risks and have a process for 
incident response and recovery in case of a security breach. They should also have procedures in place to ensure the 
protection of sensitive customer information, and to comply with standards and regulations such as ISO27001, GDPR 
and PCI-DSS when seen necessary by QNB- Egypt.
17.    Product Safety and Quality
Qatar National Bank (QNB) is committed to providing its customers with safe and high-quality products and services. 
As such, QNB expects its third-party suppliers to adhere to the highest standards of product safety and quality 
throughout their operations. This includes compliance with all applicable laws and regulations, implementing robust 
quality control measures, and providing accurate and transparent information about the products and services they provide.
QNB expects its suppliers to take all necessary steps to ensure that their products and services meet or exceed

QNB expects its suppliers to take all necessary steps to ensure that their products and services meet or exceed 
industry standards, meet the needs and expectations of customers, and are free from defects or hazards. This includes 
performing regular inspections, testing, and audits to ensure that products and services meet safety and quality 
standards. In addition, suppliers must have a process in place to address and resolve customer complaints and safety 
concerns in a timely and effective manner.
18.    Financial Integrity
Third party suppliers should ensure that they maintain solvency, practice financial prudence with appropriate 
governance and keep accurate financial records of all matters related to their business with QNB in accordance with 
standard accounting practices such as Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) or International Financial 
Reporting Standards (IFRS).
19.    T ax Transparency and Compliance
All Third-party suppliers are required to maintain full tax transparency and ensure compliance with all applicable 
international and local tax laws.
Besides that, adherence to all applicable laws and legislation and any amendments that may occur to them in the 
future, which are issued by the competent authority regarding the issuance of laws and legislation at the past and at 
the future. 
Also, there is no violation of the applicable laws that would have a negative impact on suppliers that prevents them

20.   Business Continuity
QNB is committed to managing, controlling and ensuring service continuity throughout its business operations. 
Third party suppliers are expected to maintain appropriate management and control frameworks to ensure business 
resiliency practices are appropriate and fit for purpose in relation to the services and products they deliver to QNB.
QNB expects its suppliers to manage continuity risk to ensure availability of critical services to QNB during a 
disastrous event. It is a requirement that each supplier maintains a comprehensive business continuity program 
that addresses the loss of facilities, technology, human capital or suppliers necessary to support QNB. QNB expects 
suppliers to perform regular BCP/DR to appraise their resiliency and identify potential issues that would impact 
continuous service delivery to QNB. Suppliers are expected to share these plans and test results as requested.
21.   Supply Chain Risk
Where the provisions of goods and services or activities to QNB are subcontracted or materially reliant / dependent 
upon other fourth or fifth parties (etc.), we expect our third parties to ensure any of their relevant third party supply 
chain risks are identified, assessed and managed through a defined framework, any changes or risks impacting the 
supply of services or products to QNB should be escalated in a timely manner to QNB. W e encourage our third party

supply of services or products to QNB should be escalated in a timely manner to QNB. W e encourage our third party 
suppliers to extend the principles of the TPSCC through their supply chain.
22.    Transparency and Communication
QNB values transparency and open communication with its third-party suppliers. QNB expects its suppliers to 
be transparent and communicative throughout their business dealings with QNB, providing accurate and timely 
information about their operations and any changes to their business, and being responsive to any questions or 
concerns raised by QNB.
Suppliers should have a dedicated point of contact for QNB and must have a system in place to effectively 
communicate with QNB and provide relevant information or reports as required. This includes providing regular 
updates on their operations, performance, and any changes to their business that may affect their relationship with QNB.
23.    Adherence
This code is incorporated by reference into the contract with the supplier and is legally binding. Any breach of the 
mandatory requirements set forth in this code may result in actions being invoked against the supplier in accordance 
with the terms and conditions of the contract. In cases of non-compliance, the supplier may be required to implement 
corrective action plans to remediate the issue. Additionally, we reserve the right to conduct re-audits to verify that 
improvements have been made and sustained.
T erms and conditions apply

24.    Reporting, Raising Concerns and Whistleblowing
QNB expects its suppliers to help our business succeed and promote our values and high professional standards, 
including our commitment to do the right thing by our various stakeholders. QNB is committed to fostering an 
environment where our third-party suppliers and sub-contractors can raise any concerns about any actual or
suspected breach of this code or actual or suspected misconduct.
QNB’ s TPSCC is available on QNB’ s website.

QNB Group has and continues to achieve leading positions in the global banking 
sector. Its sustainable profitable growth has made it a dominant market player, and 
the integrity, transparency, and professionalism of its staff, as well as its strong 
commitment to social responsibility and the high competence and broad futuristic

QNB Group is also nearing the achievement of its vision to become a leading bank in the

Code of Ethics and Conduct in their work and their daily lives.
As a member of QNB Group, you will work along this select group of professionals who 
have dedicated their time and efforts to supporting the QNB corporate values and Code 
of Ethics, which you will also be expected to follow at all times, whether in the office or 
outside it. T o help you achieve this, we have put together a number of policy statements,

Purpose
The Code of Ethics and Conduct is 
considered to be an integral part of  
QNBʼ s policies and forms a framework 
and guidance for the conduct of business.

suppliers, and regulators.

staff (referred to as ‘we’), and those

times.

Corporate Social Responsibility
Wherever we do business we work on building stronger and more inclusive communities.  Our efforts are focused on the most disadvantaged through projects that deliver basic welfare, improve essential infrastructure and provide relief in emergencies. The Bank realized the importance of its role in supporting the social development process, realizing the correlation between the development of society and the success of major institutions. It is a long-term business imperative that embodies QNB business values.  Therefore, we have participated in many development projects in the following fields:

Healthcare:  QNB Supports the healthcare sector by supporting institutions that provide free medical services through donating the necessary medical equipment and financing the setting up of medical units in public and university hospitals, in addition to implementing medical convoys in villages and destitute areas in order to improve the quality of provided medical services, and to reduce the waiting lists. The bank supports also in providing medical services in the marginalized areas which suffer from lack of healthcare out of the bank’s belief in the importance of providing support to all the unprivileged people that suit their living circumstances. Moreover, the importance of participating in veterinary convoys to improve animal production was introduced being an important source of income for many rural families. 
Education:  QNB supports the educational sector by supporting educational institutions especially primary schools in Upper Egypt and Delta. The Bank developed many schools and provided school supplies to improve and deliver the high educational services, in addition to providing scholarships for the outstanding students in some universities and financing the construction of laboratories in technical institutes and universities, as well as sponsoring the scientific events related to educational and scientific research and providing several financial literacy sessions to spread the concept of financial inclusion.

Social support:  QNB participates in raising the standard of living for the unprivileged people by supporting them to meet their needs without discrimination through many social development projects. These projects include all categories embracing youth, woman and people with special needs and provide all social support activities: 
    Potable Water supply and water quality improvement:   QNB participates in delivering clean drinking water to Houses of unprivileged families, in addition to the bank’s participation in providing potable drinking water and improving its quality in the destitute villages by renovating and extending water network projects.
    Improving the residential Environment:  QNB participates in many projects which aim at improving the residential environment believing in the importance of providing decent, safe and healthy housing for the neediest families through the participation in roofing, renovating and improving the houses’ efficiency.
    Youth and Woman Economic Empowerment: Out of the bank’s belief in the importance of supporting women and youth and empowering them economically, the bank provides micro projects and income generating projects to guarantee a sustainable source of income for them and their families.

Corporate Social Responsibility
Wherever we do business we work on building stronger and more inclusive communities.  Our efforts are focused on the most disadvantaged through projects that deliver basic welfare, improve essential infrastructure and provide relief in emergencies. The Bank realized the importance of its role in supporting the social development process, realizing the correlation between the development of society and the success of major institutions. It is a long-term business imperative that embodies QNB business values.  Therefore, we have participated in many development projects in the following fields:

Healthcare:  QNB Supports the healthcare sector by supporting institutions that provide free medical services through donating the necessary medical equipment and financing the setting up of medical units in public and university hospitals, in addition to implementing medical convoys in villages and destitute areas in order to improve the quality of provided medical services, and to reduce the waiting lists. The bank supports also in providing medical services in the marginalized areas which suffer from lack of healthcare out of the bank’s belief in the importance of providing support to all the unprivileged people that suit their living circumstances. Moreover, the importance of participating in veterinary convoys to improve animal production was introduced being an important source of income for many rural families. 
Education:  QNB supports the educational sector by supporting educational institutions especially primary schools in Upper Egypt and Delta. The Bank developed many schools and provided school supplies to improve and deliver the high educational services, in addition to providing scholarships for the outstanding students in some universities and financing the construction of laboratories in technical institutes and universities, as well as sponsoring the scientific events related to educational and scientific research and providing several financial literacy sessions to spread the concept of financial inclusion.

    Improving the residential Environment:  QNB participates in many projects which aim at improving the residential environment believing in the importance of providing decent, safe and healthy housing for the neediest families through the participation in roofing, renovating and improving the houses’ efficiency.
    Youth and Woman Economic Empowerment: Out of the bank’s belief in the importance of supporting women and youth and empowering them economically, the bank provides micro projects and income generating projects to guarantee a sustainable source of income for them and their families.

UN Sustainable Development Goals and external commitments
UN Sustainable Development Goals and external commitments
QNB Group is committed to international frameworks and guidelines, in addition to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals and has developed sustainability strategy in line with these national and international frameworks. The Group reports its performance publicly and in accordance with the widely established Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards.
United Nations Sustainable Development Goals
The United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are the principle global framework for sustainability. Their aim is to protect the planet, end poverty, fight inequalities and ensure prosperity.
Launched in 2016, through to 2030, the 17 goals are underpinned by 169 detailed targets and apply to every nation …and every sector.  Cities, businesses, schools, organisations, all are challenged to act.

To achieve the Sustainable Development Goals, it is estimated between $5-7 trillion dollars of annual investment is needed across sectors and industries, between now and 2030.
United Nations Environment Programme Finance Initiative “UNEP FI”
QNB became a member of the United Nations Environment Programme Finance Initiative “UNEP FI” and a signatory to the Principles of Responsible Banking “PRB”. Being a specialized framework for ensuring that the strategy and practices of signatory banks align with the Sustainable Development Goals and the Paris Climate Agreement.
QNB ’s membership in the UNEP FI stems from its belief in the importance of the role of sustainable finance. The membership supports global and national sustainable commitments and goals. The UNEP FI encourages and promotes financial institutions to create a sustainable financial sector and facilitates knowledge development and sharing to help shape and scale up sustainable finance.
 
United Nations Global Compact
The United Nations Global Compact (UNGC), the world’s largest corporate sustainability initiative, consists of ten principles to promote better business practices in the areas of human rights, labor, environment and anti-corruption. 
In 2019, QNB Group joined the UNGC and committed to making the principles part of its strategy, culture and day-to-day operations. In support of public accountability and transparency, QNB Group reports on progress annually.

QNB Sustainability Framework and Strategy
Our sustainability framework consists of three pillars; sustainable finance, sustainable operations and beyond banking. All three pillars contribute to QNB ’s goal of ensuring sustainable financial performance, through reducing risks, opening up new business opportunities and strengthening our brand. Under each pillar we have identified the issues most material to our business and abided by a Group-wide policy statements to establish common global standards across the organisation.

Sustainable Finance
Sustainable finance integrates environmental, social and governance (ESG) criteria into our business and investment decisions for the lasting benefit of our clients and society as a whole. Embedding sustainability practices within our lending, investments, products and services, is the most significant way in which we can support national and global sustainable development goals. Moreover, it enables us to manage risks to our own financial performance and profit from business opportunities emerging from the transition to a greener, more inclusive economy.
Material topics within ‘Sustainable Finance’;
Sustainable investment, lending, products and services
Supporting SMEs and entrepreneurship
Financial inclusion, accessibility and financial education
Digital innovation and transformation
Responsible customer communication and marketing
Customer privacy and data security
Customer experience
Sustainable Operations
Sustainable operations refer to managing our direct ESG impacts, ensuring we operate ethically and efficiently. Our approach to improving sustainable operations is to measure, manage and report performance in alignment with the criteria set by QNB Group and guidance on ESG reporting. This places particular emphasis on strong corporate governance, respecting the human rights of our employees and suppliers, and minimising the carbon emissions associated with our operations.

Sustainability Management at QNB
Sustainability has become one of the most pressing topics impacting our society today. This includes environmental aspects, such as climate change and resource scarcity, social aspects, such as human rights, financial inclusion and data privacy, and corporate governance aspects, such as board composition, anti-corruption and ethical business practices. Collectively, these are commonly referred to as ESG (Environment, Social, and Governance). 
There is now increasing demand from investors, customers, regulators and our own employees for greater transparency of our approach to ESG issues. And we recognise the significant contribution QNB can make to society by adopting business practices to address these, especially through our financing activities. Furthermore, we believe that a proactive approach to sustainability strengthens QNB ’s business resilience and supports sustainable financial performance.

1- المقدمةـــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــ 2 
2- إطار الحوكمة ف ي بنك التنمية الصناعية ــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــ 3

تقرير الحوكمة لعام2019 2 
 
1 - المقدمة 
 يلتزم بنك التنمية الصناعية إلتزاماً تاماً بقيم الحوكمة الرشيدة كخيار أساسي لتوطيد 
الثقة مع أصحاب المصالح من خلال تبني أعلى معايير الحوكمة المؤسسية و 
ترجمتها إلى ممارسات ملموسة و مترسخة في أعمال البنك و توجهاته الإستراتيجية. 
 
 يحرص بنك التنمية الصناعية على الإلتزام بأفضل ممارسات الحوكمة في سائر 
عملياته من تنظيم العلاقة بين الأطراف الرئيسية في البنك ، و خصوصاً  المساهمين 
والإدارة التنفيذية للبنك و مجلس الإدارة ، حيث تحدد مسئوليات كل طرف و حقوقه 
مع تعزيز مبادئ الشفافيه و المسائلة و المسئولية و المساواة من خلال إعتماد 
سياسات و نظم للعمل مستمدة من قواعد و معايير الحوكمة المعمول بها محليا   و 
يتماشى معها من أفضل ممارسات الحوكمة الدولية. 
 
 كما يضع مجلس الإدارة تطبيق الحوكمة على رأس أولويات المجلس من خلال 
إقراره إطار الحوكمة لدى بنك التنمية الصناعية ، وتحديد لوائح العمل لكيفية قيام 
المجلس بالأدوار الموكلة إليه ، و إشرافه على الهياكل و إطار الحوكمة ، فكل قطاع 
و كل موظف في البنك يعد مسئولاً عن العمل بموجب قيم البنك التي يتم قياس 
سلوكيات و ممارسات الأعمال بناءً عليها في ظل ممارسات الحوكمة الرشيدة. 
 
 و لذا فإن بنك التنمية الصناعية ينظر إلى الإلتزام بالقواعد والأحكام التي تضبط  
حوكمة البنوك بإعتباره مطلب يلزم الوفاء به ، و يعتبره جزءاً  لا يتجزأ من نظام 
البنك ، و يتم تحديث و تعديل أنظمة و إجراءات "بنك التنمية الصناعية" ليتماشى 
مع تعليمات البنك المركزي المصري للحوكمة فيما يتعلق بالعديد من الأمور ذات 
الصلة على سبيل المثال  :  إنعقاد الجمعية العمومية و مجالس الإدارة  و تشكيل

تقرير الحوكمة لعام2019 3 
 
2 - إطار الحوكمة في بنك التنمية الصناعية 
 يؤمن بنك التنمية الصناعية أن تطبيق الحوكمة الجيدة تسهل الإدارة الفعالة و 
الريادة في مجال الأعمال مما يحقق نجاح البنك على المدى الطويل. 
 
  يتفانىبنك التنمية الصناعية في تطبيق معايير الحوكمة الرشيدة بشكل يتفق مع 
اللوائح والقوانين المحلية المعمول بها. كما يتبع أفضل الممارسات الدولية الصادرة 
عن لجنة بازل بخصوص الرقابة المصرفية ، فضلاً  على المؤسسات الدولية 
الأخرى . 
 
 يشمل مفهوم الحوكمة مجموعة من العلاقات بين إدارة البنك و مجلس الإدارة و
أصحاب المصالح الأخرى ، مما يؤثر على سمعة البنك ، كما يسهم تطبيق الحوكمة 
في تحفيز كافة الموظفين بالبنك بإدارة المهام التشغيلية و الإدارية بكفاءة عالية و 
الذي بدوره يؤدي إلى نمو البنك و زيادة حصته في السوق المصرفي. 
 
 وفقاً لتعليمات الحوكمة الصادرة عن البنك المركزي المصري يتم فصل أدوار 
ومسئوليات مجلس الإدارة عن مهام الإدارة التنفيذية ، حيث يتولى مجلس الإدارة 
الإشراف العام على المجموعة ويقدم التوجيه الإستراتيجي من خلال الموافقة على 
المبادرات والسياسات والأهداف الإستراتيجية وذلك لضمان إتباع و تنفيذ المتطلبات 
القانونية والتنظيمية وذلك للوصول إلى الإلتزام  بالمعايير الدولية. 
 
 تطبيقاً لتعليمات الحوكمة ، قام مجلس إدارة بنك التنمية الصناعية بإعتماد هيكل 
تنظيمي يعكس مبدأ الشفافيه و المسائلة والفصل بين المهام من خلال إرساء نظام 
فعال من الضوابط بما يضمن الإشراف المستمر و الرقابة الفعالة على مختلف 
المستويات الوظيفية ، علاوة على ذلك تم إعتماد سياسة جديدة لتقييم ومراقبة الأداء 
لكافة المستويات الوظيفية مما قد يسهم في بذل العناية و الكفاءة العالية في تنفيذ
