Prioritising Staff Health 
ADCB-Egypt cares about the safety of its 
staff. Therefore, ADCB-Egypt always seeks to 
ensure that its working environment is safe and 
conducive to their overall health and well-being. 
Currently, ADCB–Egypt deploys a Medical 
Insurance Policy that covers all employees, 
including annual medical coverage and savings 
insurance.
In addition, the COVID-19 pandemic forced 
the Bank to take extraordinary measures to 
ensure that all its functions are carrying out 
their duties and responsibilities while reducing 
the risk of spreading infection. Therefore, 
the Bank’s response to COVID-19 included a 
dedicated Working from Home policy, in which 
all employees received laptops to enable working 
from home and allow them to remain productive. 
E-meetings were also often held instead of 
physical ones, and staff capacity on-premises has 
decreased by 50%.
Furthermore, as an additional response to the 
pandemic, actions were taken to mitigate and 
manage various health risks, including raising 
awareness on hygiene protocols and enforcing 
hygiene procedures, providing face masks, 
gloves, and sanitizers, and ensuring that all 
people entering the Bank were wearing masks 
and checked with handheld thermometers. The 
teams also executed a weekly deep clean plan, 
maintaining constant communication with the 
CBE’s Security Division. In addition, a vaccination 
program was also conducted for employees, their 
families, and contractors dealing with the Bank.

Ensuring Safety Across the Bank’s Premises
ADCB-Egypt’s Security Division maintains 
a smoke-free environment via continuous 
monitoring and coordination with the HR 
Department. Fire hazards are also mitigated 
by fire prevention, control of combustibles, 
ignition sources, human acts and housekeeping 
maintenance, continuous monitoring and 
maintenance of escape routes, and continuous 
testing and maintenance of the detection and 
alarm systems. In addition, sprinkler systems, 
automatic extinguishers, and fire hose reels are 
regularly monitored, and manual fire extinguishers 
are appropriately distributed. Mock fire drills are 
also carried out and reported.
First aid kits are periodically monitored and 
resupplied to ensure availability in the case of any 
emergency. The Security Division also responds 
to all risks from force majeure (acts of nature) to 
minimise damage and ensure the continuity of 
business operations.

individual can effectively contribute to the 
national economy as part of a highly skilled and

Learning and  
Development
We support our employees’ skill development, 
career advancement, and workplace success.
Why It Matters
Based on needs analysis, the Bank has 
successfully combined Technical Professional 
Banking, Behavioural Training, and Mandatory 
Training across physical and digital channels. 
Furthermore, with the launch of the new learning 
platform, ADCB-Egypt has given its employees 
access to organisational knowledge, practical 
guidance, and best practices on a full range of 
relevant topics. The Bank clearly sees benefits 
behind innovation and expects to further leverage 
digital tools and capacities to empower its 
employees to be experts in their fields.
Our Approach and Progress
Fostering a Workplace Culture of Continuous 
Learning 
The Bank continuously develops its employee 
development approach, including its employees’ 
succession planning strategy. ADCB–Egypt has 
also adopted a Learning Management System 
(LMS), which gives employees access to more 
than 1,400 e-Learning programs. Training 
sessions are delivered both online and physically. 
Furthermore, a staff recognition program has 
been launched, focussing on service excellence.
ADCB-Egypt’s Learning and Development 
Team also maintains a full training plan based 
on the needs analysis conducted across the 
Bank’s functions and teams. The training plan 
incorporates three main categories: Technical 
Professional Banking, Behavioural Training, and 
Mandatory Training.

access funds that are then used, which helps 
support and drive economic growth. Therefore, 
the banking sector is critical to the proper 
functioning of the economy, and corporate 
governance is key to the safety and soundness of 
the industry.

coherent Governance Framework operating up 
to the highest international standards of good 
corporate governance. Clear Group guidance 
paired with a strong local vision and dedication 
has allowed ADCB-Egypt to stand behind its 
responsible banking commitments while ensuring 
effective operations and sound decision-making.
ADCB-Egypt believes in and is committed to good 
corporate governance to provide a basis for its 
future development and corporate performance, 
to support trust in its activities as a recipient 
of depositors’ funds and shareholders’ capital,

development. The Bank’s governance structure

On implementing its functions, the Bank’s 
management may draw on internal 
multidisciplinary committees, as the Bank, 
within the Governance Program, has formed 
several committees, each with its own Terms of 
Reference. The committees’ meetings are valid 
only if there is a quorum, including the Committee 
Head or deputy. However, a representative shall 
be assigned to attend the meeting if any member 
is absent.

Board Independence
Board independence is vital as it creates a 
balance within the Board and ensures conflicts 
of interest are resolved while ensuring social 
interests are factored into decision-making, 
increasing the executive team’s efficiency. As per 
the CBE Corporate Governance regulations and 
standards, the Chairperson and CEO should be 
in different positions so that no individual can 
hold both positions simultaneously. At the same 
time, the Bank’s Board should have a maximum 
of two Executive Directors, while the rest are 
Non-Executive. In addition, two of the Board 
members should be independent and can hold 
their positions for a maximum of six years over 
two terms. ADCB–Egypt also complies with the

Board of Directors and committees oversee the 
Bank’s Management Team to ensure it does not 
engage in any activity that could be perceived as

Bank’s gift-giving, disclosure, compliance, and

sign a Conflict-of-Interest Disclosure commitment

and conflict-of-interest assessments are 
undertaken with all new employees before 
onboarding.

with the established guidelines. However, if 
compliance violations occur, the department will

misconduct through a dedicated email address 
and a hotline number.

places a high priority on risk management, 
while the Bank as a whole places a strong 
emphasis on preserving our client’s privacy 
and personal data.

The contemporary world puts risk management, 
cybersecurity, and data privacy at the centre 
of every organisation’s concern. ADCB-Egypt 
recognises comprehensive risk oversight and 
mitigation, cyberliteracy, and protection of 
customer data as central concerns. Therefore, 
the Bank keeps building one of the most 
technologically advanced and rigorous 
frameworks to ensure it is well protected from 
whatever comes next.

ADCB-Egypt has developed and adopted policies 
and processes to protect the Bank’s systems, data, 
and customers against cyberattacks, including 
customer data privacy and accessibility. In 2021, 
the Bank successfully coordinated compliance 
with the SWIFT Customer Security Protection 
Framework. 
ADCB-Egypt has also activated a New Enterprise 
Vulnerability Assessment Solution to cover all 
internal and external vulnerabilities to the Bank’s 
systems, in addition to the deployment of Phase 1 
of the Governance Risk and Compliance Tool for 
automation, tracking, and reporting of information 
security risks, as well as Firewall Monitoring, an 
auditing solution, and the Anti-DDOS Solution

ADCB–Egypt has zero tolerance for corruption and bribery and 
has established rigorous measures for Anti-Money Laundering 
(AML) and Combating the Financing of Terrorism (CFT).
Why It Matters
The number and complexity of financial crimes 
have increased in recent years, undermining 
international monetary systems, slowing 
economic growth, and resulting in enormous 
losses for firms and people worldwide. 
Additionally, corruption makes it easier for 
organized crime to flourish. Therefore, robust 
management and risk mitigation measures are 
vital to reducing and preventing financial crimes 
and their consequences.
Our Approach and Progress
ADCB-Egypt complies with international and 
national regulations related to anti-money 
laundering and terrorism financing. This includes 
setting robust policies, applying best practices, 
utilizing high technology anti-fraud systems, and 
building capacity across all relevant departments 
and stakeholders.
The Bank has also developed rigorous control 
mechanisms, procedures, and algorithms 
to identify and prevent financial crime. As a 
The Financial Crime Program is based upon

from the European Union, the United Kingdom, 
the United Nations, and the United States, as well 
as Egyptian financial crime laws and regulations.

 Tax Transparency
ADCB-Egypt acknowledges its commitment 
to transparent tax disclosures, as well as 
compliance with tax authorities and their 
requirements.
Why It Matters
Greater transparency of tax fosters greater trust 
and makes us a more responsible company. 
We must always be compliant to reduce both 
financial and reputational risks as regulators 
worldwide intensify their scrutiny and tighten 
corporate standards for tax transparency.
Our Approach and Progress
The Bank is committed to full transparency 
regarding its taxation and proactively supports 
efforts to build an effective tax system that 
works for everyone. ADCB-Egypt’s Tax Strategy 
is approved by the CFO, Managing Director, and 
CEO. It is aligned with national policies, including 
the CBE guidelines, as well as Egyptian tax laws 
for all tax types and the Egyptian Tax Authority’s 
instruction to minimise tax liabilities and risks. The 
strategy also outlines how the Bank monitors, 
controls, and provides all relevant taxation returns, 
forms, and issues according to the mandated 
frequencies under the tax laws. 
Future Outlook
ADCB–Egypt acknowledges the significance of 
maintaining transparency in its tax disclosures and 
is committed to taking all the necessary measures 
to adhere to international standards, such as 
those issued by the OECD, to combat cross-
border tax evasion, in line with the local regulatory

Introduction and Objectives of the Engagement 
Masader Environmental & Energy Services S.A.E (the ‘Assurance Provider’) has been 
engaged by the ADCB-Egypt (the ‘Reporting Organisation’) to provide Moderate 
Assurance Type 1 (the ‘Assurance’) regarding adherence to the AA1000AS v3 (2020) 
over the ADCB-Egypt ESG Report 2021 (the ‘Report’).
Scope, Subject Matter and Limitations
The subject matter of the Report is the Reporting Organisation ESG performance data 
and information for the year ended 31 December 2021. The scope of assurance is 
limited to a review of the Selected Information listed below:
• ADCB–Egypt’s ESG Management
• Stakeholder Engagement
• Materiality Assessment
The assurance process was subject to the following limitations and exclusions
• Verifying the data or information provided by ADCB-Egypt stated in the About ADCB-
Egypt section, and ADCB-Egypt’s CEO Letter.
• Appropriateness of definitions and any internal reporting criteria adopted by ADCB-
Egypt for its disclosures.
• Appropriateness of any new commitments and objectives established and 
communicated by ADCB-Egypt.
• Content of external websites or documents linked from the Report and ADCB Group.
We have not been engaged to:
• Verify any statement indicating intention, opinion, belief and/or aspiration of ADCB-

Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank - Egypt (ADCB Egypt) takes 
pride in presenting its Environmental, Social, and Governance 
(ESG) report for the year 2023. This comprehensive report 
demonstrates our dedication and commitment to ethical 
business conduct and our alignment with the sustainability 
strategy and policy of Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank PJSC.

economy, supported by strategic enablers.

actions, and aims to increase our transparency to all 
stakeholders. Continuing our commitment, we will ensure all 
our stakeholders stay informed about our achievements and 
ongoing progress.

the reporting period from January 1st to December 31st,

company, Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank PJSC, are speciﬁcally

Accounting Standards Board (SASB) ‘Industry Standards,’ 
and the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures 
(TCFD) recommendations. It also presents the Bank’s 
achievements in line with Egypt’s Vision 2030 and the UN 
Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

ADCB Egypt CEO letter
Financial Resilience Strategic Growth and 
response to Economic Challenges
As we reﬂect on 2023, it is with a clear perspective on the dynamic 
challenges and strategic advancements that ADCB Egypt has 
navigated throughout the year to achieve successfully the set 
strategic milestones. Our unyielding dedication to integrating with 
the ADCB Group and adhering to the Central Bank of Egypt’s 
directives has been central to our operations.
In response to the macro-economic headwinds, ADCB Egypt has 
shown strategic acumen, shifting our investment focus towards 
more secure assets and revising deposit interest rates in line with 
regulatory measures. These steps have ensured a steady course 
amidst economic turbulence, reﬂecting our prudent approach to 
growth and risk.
Our unwavering commitment to sustainable growth and digital

Context in Egypt
Financial landscape in Egypt
Egypt is considered to be a fast-developing nation with a 
continuous shift in economy, currency value and ﬁnancial 
markets. This coupled with the growing population, poses 
challenges related to poverty, inequality, water scarcity and 
air pollution. The Banking industry has taken responsibility 
in tackling these issues as the forefront of ﬁnancial activities. 
The Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) has embarked on increasing 
initiatives to address the nation’s growing concerns, guiding 
ﬁnancial institutions to become a solution. This is enacted by 
crafting sustainable ﬁnancial strategies that prioritise social 
and environmental risk management, responsible lending 
practices, and the promotion of green ﬁnancing.
Egypt’s position on climate change
Due to Egypt’s vulnerability to climate change, it’s vital to 
prioritise adapting to its effects alongside broader mitigation 
efforts. The initial 2011 National Strategy focused on 
adapting to climate change and reducing disaster risks. 
Egypt reafﬁrmed its commitment to tackling climate change 
by spreading awareness on the issues at the global level at 
COP27 in Sharm El Sheikh, promoting the UN SDGs and 
spreading awareness on the direct over-looming climate 
change impacts facing Egypt and similar developing nations.

for a comprehensive strategy until 2050 to address climate

Sustainable ﬁnance in Egypt
Egypt believes that sustainable ﬁnance will be one of the 
key drivers for the 2030 vision. Sustainable ﬁnance involves 
diverse ﬁnancial tools, sourced from public and private 
sectors, to address climate change, social, and environmental 
issues. Funding comes from institutional investors, banks, 
regulators, central banks, and international ﬁnance 
institutions. Options include inclusive loans, subsidies, risk 
insurance, green bonds, and various mechanisms. 
In 2023, Egypt updated its Nationally Determined Contribution 
(NDC 2015-2030) to align with developmental and climate 
change policies, including Sustainable Development Strategy: 
Egypt’s Vision 2030, Long-Term Low Emission Development 
Strategy 2050 (LT-LEDS), and National Climate Change 
Strategy 2050 (NCCS), among others. This update integrates 
strategies like the Integrated Sustainable Energy Strategy 2035 
and National Water Resources Plan (2017-2037). The revision 
includes a review and update of mitigation and adaptation 
measures, additional actions categorised by sector, and 
projections of business-as-usual (BAU) GHG emissions by 
2030 for three sectors, with quantiﬁcation of GHG reductions 
from ongoing and planned mitigation projects, creating a newly 
adapted plan to match current challenges.

encompass the establishment of independent sustainability and sustainable ﬁnance departments within each bank, integrating

The CBE unveiled the National Financial Inclusion Strategy 
(2022-2025), aimed at bolstering ﬁnancial inclusion. This 
strategic plan aims to widen access to formal ﬁnancial 
services for underserved populations, boost ﬁnancial literacy, 
fortify ﬁnancial infrastructure, and foster inclusion among 
women and PwD. Collaborating with government entities,

Materiality assessment
In 2023, ADCB Egypt recalled the list of material topics identiﬁed during the materiality assessment process in 2021. Materiality assessments previously conducted were comprehensive of stakeholder engagements to identify, assess and prioritise the list of topics that are 
most impactful and signiﬁcant to ADCB Egypt’s operations over 2023.
STEP 1  
Identify a pool of potential  
ESG material issues
STEP 2  
Engage with stakeholders  
and gather their insight
STEP 3  
Assess and prioritise material topics
STEP 4  
Review and validate material topics
We identiﬁed industry-speciﬁc topics based on global 
standards (GRI, SASB) and ESG rating agencies. The 
list was then narrowed to focus on areas relevant to the 
national context in Egypt and align with ADCB Egypt’s 
business activities and strategic priorities.
Expanding on the identiﬁed topics, we conducted 
surveys, workshops, and interviews with internal 
stakeholders, including employees, department heads, 
and C-suite members, to gain insights into the most 
signiﬁcant topics.
 ~ Internal- We surveyed, conducted workshops and 
discussed material issues with top management
 ~ External- We analysed national strategies, 
engaged with the CBE through surveys, 
and considered recent initiatives, mandates, 
and updates in 2023 such as Sustainable 
Finance, People with Disabilities, 
Financial Inclusion, and MSMEs.
Subsequently, we prioritised topics by analysing survey

Ultimately, we thoroughly reviewed and validated ADCB

proposed course of action for each one.

resonate with our sustainability objectives, such as renewable energy and gender equality.

While the transition to sustainable investing presents certain challenges, such as evaluating less tangible criteria and potentially 
foregoing opportunities in high-emitting sectors, the long-term beneﬁts far outweigh the short-term costs. Major global shifts 
in policy, resource availability, and consumer and investor preferences are putting fossil fuel-reliant business models at risk. In 
contrast, sustainable sectors such as renewable energy and green technology offer lucrative growth prospects.
From this ﬁscal year onwards, we are committed to fully divesting from coal and tar sands extraction and tripling our investments 
in climate change solutions by 2025. We have also appointed an independent advisory panel to audit our portfolio quarterly and 
provide guidance on strengthening our ESG integration approach. While progress will take time, our goal is for 100% of AUM 
to comprise only sustainable investments by the end of the decade. Such determined actions are needed from all segments of 
society if we are to achieve a just and prosperous low-carbon economy and safeguard our planet for future generations.
In 2023, ADCB Egypt made signiﬁcant strides in incorporating ESG considerations into our ﬁnancial strategies and operations.

challenges.

our operations and supporting our customers in their transition to a lower-carbon economy. The Treasury Group is aligning the 
Bank’s investment strategy with macro-trends to both mitigate ﬁnancial risks and unlock new areas for return. Consequently, 
Treasury is supporting newly launched innovative sustainable ﬁnance solutions for both corporate and individual customers. 
Additionally, ADCB Egypt has participated in Green Euro Bonds to encourage impact green ﬁnancing and investment. This 
comprehensive approach reﬂects our dedication to sustainable development, following in ADCB Group’s footsteps and their

Overall, I am proud of the progress our company has made in incorporating ESG considerations into our ﬁnancial strategies and

and social risks, ADCB can mitigate potential negative 
impacts on the environment and society that could arise from 
operations or ﬁnancing activities, comply with regulations, 
partner with socially responsible investors, and contribute 
positively to the communities it serves.

In alignment with ADCB Group ESRM policy, ADCB Egypt 
aims into implementation its ESRM policy deﬁning the 
principles from the identiﬁcation, monitoring and reporting of 
the E&S risks . This should enable ADCB Egypt to conduct 
enhanced due diligence in sectors with signiﬁcant social or 
environmental impact and to achieve the Bank’s objective 
to increase its sustainable ﬁnance portfolio to 15% by 2030. 
The current status quo of ADCB Egypt is a widely diversiﬁed 
portfolio across a range of sectors, with no exposure higher 
than 30% for one sector.

Risks identiﬁcation
ADCB identiﬁes risks and opportunities related to environmental and social factors, which could impact its internal business 
operations and counterparties. This approach ensures the Bank is equipped to mitigate potential adverse effects on its operations 
and expand sustainable opportunities. 
ADCB Egypt is aware that environmental risks can have adverse effects on the Bank’s premises, reputation, and credit exposures 
linked to climate change and environmental degradation. On the other hand, social risks pertain to potential negative impacts on 
ADCB Egypt’s business and reputation stemming from its ﬁnancing activities. These risks arise from factors, such as human rights 
violations, unfair labour practices, unsafe working conditions, and mishandling of customer privacy. One illustrative example is the 
risk of default or ﬁnancial loss due to exposure to counterparties facing potential ﬁnes and reputational damage from workplace 
fatalities and incidents 
Concurrently, ADCB Egypt is attuned to the opportunities presented by sustainable projects, particularly within the emerging green 
markets. Acknowledging these challenges and opportunities signiﬁcantly inﬂuences the decision-making
.

Climate risk assessment 
The metrics used to assess climate-related risks adhere to the 
established norms in organisational greenhouse gas (GHG) 
accounting and following the WBCSD/WRI GHG Protocol, 
we have diligently incorporated all seven Kyoto Protocol 
greenhouse gases in our assessment, wherever applicable 
and signiﬁcant. Our evaluation methodology employs 
benchmarking to gauge the performance of our organisation 
over time and to compare it with counterparts in the same 
industry. This process not only enables us to assess our 
standing but also helps identify industry best practices and 
potential areas for enhancement. Speciﬁcally, we utilise Scope 
1 & 2 carbon emission intensities (per Full-Time Equivalent 
employee and per square meter) for national benchmarking 
of ADCB Egypt’s performance. Additionally, the intensity of 
electricity consumption per square meter serves as a metric for 
assessing our performance on a broader international scale.

ADCB Egypt’s branches use municipal water for drinking 
and sanitary purposes. Since these branches are located 
in residential areas, the water bills are usually consolidated 
across all building users. The Bank has installed water 
meters for some branches and is currently working on 
installing them for the remaining ones. All ADCB Egypt 
branches consumed a total of 3,750 m3 of water in 
2023. To further reduce water consumption, ADCB Egypt 
equipped all its branches with water-efﬁcient faucets 
and installed a wastewater recycling system in the head 
ofﬁce building in Mohandessin. The head ofﬁce building 
consumed a total of 12.065.000 mega liters of municipal 
water in 2023.

or track the amount of general ofﬁce waste. However, 
ADCB Egypt is working on developing a corporate-wide 
waste management policy and plan that will establish 
suitable methods for segregating, storing, collecting, and 
disposing of waste across all of its branches.

core strategy.

chunk_text:
[توثيق مرجعي للوكيل الذكي: تقرير بنك: بنك أبو ظبي التجاري ADCB - المستند: ADCB-Egypt-ESG-Report-2023.pdf - موضع: 55]
ADCB Egypt is strongly dedicated to empowering PwD, striving for their complete inclusion in the Banking sector. Substantial measures 
have been taken by ADCB Egypt to offer equal opportunities and convenient access to its services for PwD. ADCB Egypt engaged in 
extensive consultation exercises and solicited the expertise of several specialised organisation in previous years to tailor packages to 
support creating a well-informed accessible ﬁnancial institution. Accordingly, several improvements were made to address PwD needs.
Braille documents
ADCB Egypt has made banking documents accessible in Braille, providing visually impaired customers with the ability 
to independently access and comprehend the content without relying on assistance from others. This initiative fosters 
autonomy and privacy, empowering visually impaired individuals to manage their ﬁnances with ease and conﬁdence, 
without any intervention. 
Sign language
ADCB Egypt acknowledges the signiﬁcance of clear communication and has provided specialised training in sign 
language for its customer service employees. This enables the Bank’s staff to effectively communicate with hearing-
impaired individuals, addressing their inquiries comprehensively. By being proﬁcient in sign language, employees 
ensure that hearing-impaired customers receive the same level of service and support as any other customer. This 
commitment fosters an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and understood.

commitment fosters an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and understood.
Accessible branches
ADCB Egypt conducted a comprehensive meeting with PwDs to gain insight into their distinct banking needs. In response, 
ADCB Egypt has established branches with enhanced accessibility features for PwDs. There are 13 branches now equipped 
with entrances specially designed for wheelchair use, facilitating easier access to banking services for customers with 
mobility disabilities. These modiﬁcations underscore the Bank’s dedication to eliminating physical barriers and establishing 
a welcoming environment for individuals facing mobility challenges. We are committed to ensuring that individuals with 
disabilities can independently access and beneﬁt from our services, promoting inclusivity and equal opportunities for all.
Accessible ATMs
In an effort to promote inclusivity, ADCB Egypt has 56 ATMs speciﬁcally designed to cater to the needs of PwDs. All 
ADCB Egypt ATMs offer accessibility support such as voice reading feature for visually impaired customers This initiative 
underscores ADCB Egypt’s ongoing commitment to leading the way in integrating PWDs into the Banking system.

Case study: 
ERADA 
Eye on efforts for empowering PWD and  
the dedicated ERADA package
In 2023, the Bank has seen an increase in the number of 
Erada ﬁnancial inclusion package holders by 50%. This 
increase reﬂects the attention given by the Bank to the 
empowerment of PWD since its rebranding in 2020 and 
efforts along its vision “Empowerment via inclusion. 
The efforts are around two pillars: ﬁnancial inclusion 
through the Erada Package and corporate social 
responsibility through different initiatives. 
The Erada Package
ADCB Egypt launched the Erada package in 2021, (translated 
as Willpower) and it has since become the award-winning 
primary package designed to support PWD. The package 
offers banking and non-banking features and supports the 
initiatives set by the CBE and the nation to integrate PWD’s 
into society with ease. 
This comprehensive package provides many Banking facilities 
and services to help PWD in their daily lives. The package is 
exempted from account opening fees and minimum required 
balance. The Banking beneﬁts also include the issuance of a 
“Meeza” prepaid card, and registration for all digital Banking 
services to access accounts, transfer and pay from anywhere 
and at any time and both services are offered without any 
administrative fees.
Non-Banking beneﬁts are also offered and they include the 
issuance of medical discount cards with a wide coverage 
network around the country, discounts on various medical

For easy access, PWD are offered the possibility to open an

Erada is an award-winning programme by ADCB Egypt

Advancing digitalisation
ADCB Egypt aims to remain the leading bank for digitalisation in Egypt, hence continuous improvements are added to our digital 
services, based on client feedback, pro-active customer satisfaction initiatives and new availing technologies. A few examples of 
some of our digitalisation enhancements are as follows:
Token Self Registration
Enables users to independently register for security tokens, enhancing account security through a self-service process.
Expired KYC Notiﬁcation
Notiﬁes users when their Know Your Customer (KYC) documentation is about to expire within the speciﬁc period set forth in 
the relevant regulations, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements.
Activate & Deactivate Debit/Prepaid Card
Allows users to activate or deactivate their debit or prepaid cards, enabling quick and secure access to funds.
Report Stolen Debit/Prepaid Card
Allows users to report a stolen card promptly, triggering necessary security measures to prevent unauthorised transactions.
Prepaid Card Reload
Enables users to add funds to their prepaid cards conveniently, ensuring uninterrupted access to ﬁnancial resources.
Enable Biometric Login
Enhances account security by allowing users to enable biometric authentication methods for login, such as ﬁngerprint or 
facial recognition.
Loyalty Points Inquiry
Provides users with the capability to check their accumulated loyalty points, promoting transparency and engagement with 
rewards programmes.

Equality, diversity and inclusion 
Why it matters
ADCB Egypt ﬁrmly believes in the power harnessed through a 
diverse employee portfolio, as the additional insights provided 
by different points of view can be considered irreplaceable. 
Our culture celebrates the diverse qualities and abilities that 
each individual brings to the team.
Our approach and progress
ADCB Egypt continuously evaluates our organisational culture, 
internal procedures and representations of diverse groups 
throughout the levels of the Bank. Diversity and inclusion are 
essential at ADCB Egypt, we uphold diversity across various 
categories such as race, gender, age, religion, and experience. 
ADCB Egypt is committed to promoting fairness to unlock the 
creative potential of the diverse workforce. 
Gender diversity 
ADCB Egypt aims to continuously provide equal opportunities 
throughout the Bank; we currently stand at 32% female 
representation, consistent from 2022. This trend is further 
reﬂected in the gender diversity in new hires which also 
stands as 32%. 
Women’s Empowerment Principles
ADCB Egypt re-afﬁrms it commitment to gender diversity, by 
promoting female empowerment and joining The Women’s 
Empowerment Principles (WEPs) by UN Women and UN Global 
Compact. This collaboration aims to drive initiatives for women’s 
empowerment, leveraging UN Women’s global expertise to drive 
positive movements towards increased gender diversity.

Maternity leave
Abiding by local laws, ADCB Egypt grants 90 days of full 
paid maternity leave, with the option to extend the leave for 
2 years of unpaid leave. The extended option however can 
only be used twice. In 2023, 23 employees went on maternity 
leave, with 100% return to work rate.

ADCB Egypt aims to continuously work on improving the 
diversiﬁcation of the Bank, by evaluating the positions across 
all sectors. We aim to promote the inclusion of women into 
senior positions, as well as increase the representation of 
underrepresented minorities in various departments. We 
are further committed to focusing on being an accessible 
employer for PwD. We aim to upgrade our facilities and 
policies, to be able to meet the national requirement of having 
5% of our employees be PwD by 2025.

Corporate governance, compliance, and code of conduct
As a robust second line of defence, we are pivotal in interweaving the threads of green banking with the fabric of green 
ﬁnance, thus upholding the integrity of our operations in the realm of environmental stewardship. Our unwavering 
commitment to transparency and accountability underscores our role in shaping the Bank’s corporate governance 
practices, ensuring that our march towards sustainability is both credible and measurable.
Embracing digitalisation and a paperless paradigm, we recognise the dual nature of this journey – fraught with challenges 
yet rich with opportunities. This digital transformation enables us to meticulously track our environmental footprint and 
optimise the use of resources, a testament to our dedication to ecological responsibility.
The long-term viability of sustainable investment is at the heart of our mission, where compliance not only safeguards but 
also propels ethical business conduct and anti-corruption measures. Through our actions, we strive to enrich the Bank’s 
value without compromising the environmental and social pillars of our economy, ensuring equitable treatment and fair 
compensation within our workforce.
As the world observes the ascendancy of green ﬁnance, with leading nations paving the way, ADCB Egypt is committed 
to expanding our Go Green initiatives. We are not merely participants but active contributors to Egypt’s sustainability

potential risks. This commitment ultimately generates greater 
value for all stakeholders. Recognising the vital role of banks

corporate governance practices at the core of industry 
security and stability. Upholding ethical standards and 
fostering trust among customers, employees, and the wider 
community, ADCB Egypt maintains a strong compliance 
culture supported by a comprehensive code of conduct.

making. ADCB Group attributes a signiﬁcant part of its 
success to its cohesive Governance Framework, which 
adheres to the highest international standards of good 
corporate governance. The Bank ﬁrmly believes in and is fully 
committed to good corporate governance as the foundation

Board Independence 
Board independence is a crucial factor in achieving a balanced 
and conﬂict-free decision-making process while considering 
societal interests. According to the Corporate Governance 
regulations and standards set by the CBE, it is required that 
the Chairperson and CEO hold separate positions to prevent 
one individual from simultaneously occupying both roles. 
Additionally, the Bank’s Board should consist of a maximum 
of two Executive Directors, with the remaining members 
being non-executive. Furthermore, at least two Board 
members should be independent and eligible to serve for two 
consecutive terms, up to a maximum of six years.
Conﬂict of Interest
A conﬂict of interest refers to circumstances that pose a risk 
of unduly inﬂuencing an ADCB Egypt employee’s professional 
judgment. It is imperative for employees to actively avoid any 
conﬂicts that may arise between the Bank, its employees, 
customers, or suppliers, regardless of whether the employee 
or their immediate family is directly involved. Even if an 
employee believes their actions would not be inﬂuenced, they 
must ensure that there is no appearance of a conﬂict. When 
a conﬂict exists or appears to exist, the responsibility for 
transactions or account management should be transferred to 
another employee. Employees have the obligation to promptly 
inform their manager of any transaction or relationship that 
could potentially create an apparent or actual conﬂict, seeking

Protecting ADCB Egypt’s assets
ADCB’s assets, including facilities, equipment, supplies, 
and its name, should only be utilised for ofﬁcial ADCB Egypt 
business. Employees are not permitted to remove any 
ADCB Egypt property from the premises without managerial 
authorisation. If authorised for off-site use, employees must 
adhere to ADCB Egypt’s security policies and procedures to 
ensure proper safeguarding of the property. All materials and 
information acquired during employment with ADCB Egypt 
are the Bank’s property, encompassing products, proposals, 
transactions, customer lists, records, marketing materials, 
and more. Upon termination, employees must return all ADCB 
Egypt property and refrain from using or disseminating such 
assets. ADCB Egypt retains the right to take decisive action 
to recover any unauthorised use or retrieval of its property.

Audit
In 2023, ADCB Egypt created a new Internal Audit Group 
manual in line with the approved IAG Charter, ADCB Group, 
and international standards. This comprehensive manual 
covers IAG processes from start to ﬁnish. Additionally, a set 
of Audit Engagement Execution Templates was developed to 
ensure standardised and high-quality outcomes. The Internal 
Audit Group Egypt (IAGE) conducts internal audits that are 
vital for assessing internal controls and risk management 
practices. Findings are reported to the Board Audit Committee, 
CEO&MD, and Bank management, with timely follow-up on 
recommendations. Quarterly reports on outstanding issues are 
also submitted to relevant senior management.
In addition, we’ve introduced a new Audit Strategy, approach, 
and methodology for 2024-2028 to make our audit process 
more effective. ADCB Egypt will perform a SWOT analysis 
and assess stakeholders to identify and prioritise key success 
factors and initiatives aligned with the Bank’s strategic goals. 
Our aim is to enhance our understanding of the control 
environment across various activities, including strategic, 
operational, ﬁnancial, credit, market, and process risks. This 
thorough approach ensures a comprehensive examination 
that aligns with the Bank’s overarching strategic objectives.
In 2023 ADCB Egypt achieved 97% of the 2023 audit plan 
despite resource challenges and unplanned increases in 
consultation and coordination activities.

Tax transparency
Why it matters
ADCB Egypt is steadfast in maintaining transparency 
standards in its tax practices, aligning closely with the 
principles upheld by the ADCB Group. Acknowledging its role 
as a contributor to the Egyptian economy and participant in 
offshore ﬁnancial service activities, ADCB Egypt recognises 
the profound impact of its corporate behaviour on various 
stakeholders, encompassing customers, shareholders, 
employees, and governments. Demonstrating a commitment 
to robust corporate values and conduct, including its taxation 
approach, the Bank ﬁrmly holds that transparency is crucial 
for fostering trust and encouraging responsible practices 
within the Banking industry.
Our approach and progress
ADCB Egypt is wholeheartedly dedicated to ensuring tax 
compliance by adhering to all relevant tax laws, rules, and 
regulations without any exceptions
Governance 
The Tax Control Framework of ADCB Group serves as a 
crucial tool for overseeing our tax matters. It encompasses 
all tax policies and procedures throughout the Group. ADCB 
Egypt aligns seamlessly with this framework.

Tax responsibilities 
ADCB Egypt’s Tax Strategy, approved by the CFO, Managing 
Director, and CEO, meticulously aligns with national guidelines 
and policies, including those of the CBE and Egyptian tax 
laws. It is crafted to comply with the directives of the Egyptian 
Tax Authority, aiming to minimise tax liabilities and associated 
risks while implementing robust tax risk management policies.
The Head of Tax at ADCB Egypt oversees the implementation 
of stringent internal controls, policies, and procedures to 
ensure effective tax management. The tax position undergoes 
conﬁrmation by external auditors, incorporating feedback 
from tax consultants.

ADCB Egypt rigorously oversees tax risk through stringent 
protocols, aligning its tax control framework with the highest 
standards. By mirroring ADCB Group’s concepts, the 
Bank effectively manages tax risks, ensuring compliance 
with relevant tax laws and regulations. This commitment 
underscores ADCB Egypt’s dedication to responsible tax 
practices and transparency in its tax affairs.
Tax planning and tax law compliance
ADCB Egypt is dedicated to achieving full compliance with 
tax obligations across all jurisdictions of operation. The 
subsidiary ensures that tax authorities receive thorough, 
accurate, and dependable information, adhering to relevant 
legislation and submitting it punctually. In alignment with 
ADCB Group standards, ADCB Egypt abstains from adopting 
tax positions that overtly contradict tax laws or administrative 
practices in the respective jurisdictions. ADCB Egypt diligently 
adheres to tax legislation, preventing evasion and taking ﬁrm 
action against involved employees. The Bank refrains from

information for the year ended 31 December 2023. The scope of assurance is limited to

At the current global rate of consumption, humans are 
consuming natural resources of the planet at a higher 
rate than it is regenerated. We would need 2 Earths to 
satisfy our needs by 2030. In order to preserve ADCB-
E’s resources, it is crucial that we reduce the carbon 
emissions. As a growing presence in the local banker 
sector, ADCB-Egypt understands its responsibilities. 
This includes conducting business from a sustainable 
perspective through the creation of progressive policies 
and procedures. ADCB-E is hereby presenting its first 
carbon footprint assessment.
About the Bank
ADCB Egypt was established in 2020 through the 
acquisition of UNB. With an aim to deliver revolutionary 
banking solutions and lead the digitization breakthrough. 
It reaches out to its customers not only through its 
highly advanced online services but also through its 
nationwide network of 46 branches and numerous 
ATMs. 
ADCB-E is actively offering a wide range of financial 
products, services and innovative digital solutions for 
Retail, Affluent customers, SMEs and Corporate at the 
highest level of service excellence and convenience. 
Committed to serving the national economy in 
alignment with Egypt’s vision 2030 and striving to be a 
responsible corporate citizen, ADCB-E creates strategic 
partnerships and invests in significant causes that will 
create positive social and economic outcomes for our 
customers and communities. Furthermore, the bank

For the purpose of accounting and reporting GHG 
emissions, the organizational boundary defines 
the businesses and operations that constitute the 
company. Companies can choose to report either 
the emissions from operations over which they have 
financial or operational control (the control approach) 
or from operations according to their share of equity 
in the operation (the equity share approach). ADCB-E 
uses the operational control approach to calculate and 
report its GHG emissions. 
Operational Boundaries
Operational boundaries determine the approach of 
incorporating the emitting activities of the reporting 
company’s business in terms of the activities that should 
be included in the calculations and how the activities 
should be classified (i.e. direct or indirect emissions).
GHG emissions fall under different Scopes; Scope 1: 
direct emissions resulting from owned or controlled 
equipment and assets, Scope 2: indirect emissions 
resulting from purchased electricity; and Scope 3: other 
significant indirect emissions resulting from the bank's 
operations.
In conformance with the GHG Protocol Corporate 
Standard and the CBE mandate, only Scope 1 and Scope 
2 emissions are mandatory to report. Nevertheless, 
ADCB-E has decided to conduct its carbon footprint 
assessment to include some Scope 3 emissions.

Definitions & TerminologyAbbreviations & Acronyms
Base Year
A base year is a reference year in the past with which current emissions can be compared. In order to 
maintain the consistency and comparability with future carbon footprints, base year emissions need to be 
recalculated when structural changes occur in the company that change the inventory boundary (such as 
acquisitions or divestments). If no changes to the boundaries of the inventory happen, the base year is not 
adjusted.
Carbon Footprint The amount of Carbon Dioxide that an individual, group, or organization lets into the atmosphere in a 
certain time frame.
CO
2e
Carbon dioxide equivalent or CO2 equivalent, abbreviated as CO2e, is a metric used to compare the 
emissions from various GHGs on the basis of their global-warming potential (GWP), by converting 
amounts of other gases to the equivalent amount of carbon dioxide with the same global warming 
potential.
Direct Emissions Greenhouse gas emissions from facilities/sources owned or controlled by a reporting company, e.g. 
generators, blowers, vehicle fleets.
Emission Factors Specific value used to convert activity data into greenhouse gas emission values.
Fugitive Emissions
Fugitive emissions are emissions of gases or vapors from pressurized equipment due to leaks and other 
unintended or irregular releases of gases, mostly from industrial activities. As well as the economic cost of

GHG Protocol Greenhouse Gas Protocol – uniform methodology used to calculate the carbon footprint of an

GWP Global Warming Potential – an indication of the global warming effect of a greenhouse gas in comparison 
to the same weight of carbon dioxide.
HVAC
HVAC (heating, ventilating, and air conditioning; also heating, ventilation, and air conditioning) is the 
technology of indoor and vehicular environmental comfort. Its goal is to provide thermal comfort and 
acceptable indoor air quality.
Indirect Emissions
Greenhouse gas emissions from facilities/sources that are not owned or controlled by the reporting 
company, but for which the activities of the reporting company are responsible, e.g. purchasing of 
electricity.
Kyoto Protocol
It operationalizes the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change by committing 
industrialized countries to limit and reduce greenhouse gases (GHG) emissions in accordance with agreed 
individual targets. 
Operational Boundary Determination of which facilities or sources of emissions will be included in a carbon footprint calculation.
Organizational Boundary Determination of which business units of an organization will be included in a carbon footprint 
calculation.

Carbon Footprint Equations
Scope 1: Direct Emissions 
Stationary Combustion 
Fuel Burning: Natural Gas
The total consumption of natural gas for ADCB-E’s headquarters was recorded on a monthly basis in m³. 
Fuel burning: Natural gas emissions (mtCO2e) = Fuel consumption (m³) x EF (mtCO2e/ m³)
Mobile Combustion 
Fuel Burning: Owned Vehicles 
ADCB-E's owned vehicles were used to transport the managers, employees, packages, etc. The type of fuel used was 
petrol. 
Fuel burning: Owned vehicles emissions (mtCO2e) = Fuel consumption (L) x EF (mtCO2e/ L)
Fugitive Emissions 
Refrigerant Leakage
Refrigeration fluids are fluids which are used to cool a space in refrigeration cycles. Each year, refrigerants (in this case 
both type R-22 and HFC-227ea) were used to re-charge the cooling systems used in each building in order to compensate 
for the leakage that happened during the operating year. All related data was found in ADCB-E’s database.
Refrigerants leakage emissions (mtCO2e) = Refrigerant leakage (kg) x EF (mtCO2e/kg)
Scope 2: Indirect emissions
Purchased Electricity
Emissions from purchased electricity are the product of the national grid emission factor and the annual electricity 
consumption of each building. The electricity consumption in ADCB-E’s was obtained from the database in kWh. The 
total electricity consumption of the year was calculated using the formula below:
Purchased electricity emissions (mtCO2e) = Electricity consumption (kWh) x EF (mtCO2e/kWh)

Purchased electricity emissions (mtCO2e) = Electricity consumption (kWh) x EF (mtCO2e/kWh)
Scope 3: Indirect emissions
Purchased Goods & Services
Office Supplies
Purchased goods are the commodities used by the different sectors. For the head office, this is the paper and ink. The 
resulting emissions fall under Scope 3. The yearly amounts of purchased goods per type have been retrieved from the 
internal data recordings, as units of items. The emissions were obtained by multiplying the emission factor per unit by the 
weight or the number of items.
Paper emissions (mtCO2e) = Weight of paper (kg) x EF (mtCO2e/kg)
Ink emissions (mtCO2e) = Number of cartridges (units) x EF of each cartridge (mtCO2e/unit)
Fuel & Energy-Related Activities (Not Included in Scope 1 & 2) 
Well-to-Tank (WTT)
WTT emissions are those that result from the production of a fuel, including resource extraction, initial processing, 
transportation, fuel production, distribution and marketing, and delivery into a consumer vehicle's fuel tank. WTT emissions 
were taken into consideration in order to reflect the full range of climatic impacts from fuel-burning activities. All fuel 
burning activities, including natural gas  & petrol consumed by ADCB-E’s head office were included in WTT emissions. For 
each amount and type of fuel burned, the general formula was applied to determine the relevant emissions.
WTT Emissions (mtCO2e) = Fuel Consumption (unit) x WTT EF (mtCO2e/unit)
Water Usage & Wastewater Treatment

WTT Emissions (mtCO2e) = Fuel Consumption (unit) x WTT EF (mtCO2e/unit)
Water Usage & Wastewater Treatment 
The emission factor for water supply and wastewater treatment is calculated by using a conversion formula, provided by 
Holding Company for Water and Wastewater (HCWW). The emissions are based on the amount of energy consumed in 
each process. The emission factors for water supply and wastewater treatment are accordingly calculated by multiplying 
the conversion factor by the electricity emission factor. At the same time, a unit analysis is performed to make sure the 
units are conforming.
Energy consumption (Wh) = Water supply/ Wastewater (m³) x Conversion formula (Wh/m³)
Water supply & treatment (mtCO2e) = Energy consumption (kWh) x EF (mtCO2e/kWh)
Business Travel 
Air Travel & Well-to-Tank (WTT) Emissions
In 2021, both international and domestic flights took place both domestically and internationally. ADCB-E's data records 
provided data of flight routes and no. of tickets. The flight distances have been obtained from airport distances calculator. 
The emissions factors were obtained from DEFRA as average passenger, flights to/from non-UK countries.
Air travel emissions (mtCO2e) = Distance travelled per passenger (p.km) x EF (mtCO2e/ p.km)

For each of the hotel stays, location and no. of nights  and residents were obtained from ADCB-E’s data records. Employees

Hotel Stays
For each of the hotel stays, location and no. of nights  and residents were obtained from ADCB-E’s data records. Employees 
stayed in Egypt and the UAE throughout the year of 2021. DEFRA is providing the emission factors per hotel night for each 
country.
Hotel stay emissions (mtCO2e) = Hotel stays (nights per country) x EF (mtCO2e/ night per country)
Rented Cars
To calculate the emissions for rented cars, no. of users, vehcicle type and distance were obtained from ADCB-E’s data 
records. All rented cars in 2021 were average passenger cars.
Rented car emissions (mtCO2e) = Distance travelled per passenger (p.km) x EF (kgCO2e/ p.km)
Employee Commuting 
Commuting & WTT
Data were calculated by estimating the distance traveled by the employees, based on the office geographical locations and 
surveys on the average distance between the employees’ homes and their work-site. The traveling distance percentages 
for commuting were estimated for 15 different distances from 5 km to 75+ km, and then multiplied by the number of 
working days in a year to get the total distance traveled.
Employees commuting emissions (mtCO2e) = Travelled distance (km) x EF (mtCO2e/ km)

I am pleased to present ADCB Egypt’s 2022 second 
ESG report reflecting on an eventful year for our Bank, 
filled with remarkable achievements and inspiring 
progress. Our commitment to Environmental, Social, and 
Governance (ESG) principles remains persistent as we 
continue to drive positive change in our operations and 
the communities we serve.
 In 2022, ADCB Egypt was recognised as one of the 
fastest-growing banks in Egypt, and sustainability is 
a crucial factor in maintaining this position. Thus, we 
understand that sustainability is not just a goal but a 
journey that requires continuous effort and dedication. 
We also recognize the inextricable relationships between 
environment, communities, public policy, economic 
growth and financial inclusion. The Bank is therefore 
adopting a holistic approach to ESG and is embedding 
sustainability in the corporate strategy.
In this context, we are active on the 4 pillars of the 
Group’s approach to ESG. For the Climate, we are 
aligning our work with the CBE’s Sustainable Finance 
principles, requirements and initiatives. As a financial 
institution, we recognise the importance of a transition

managing our influence on the environment, both in 
our operations and lending portfolio. We aim to help 
corporations and SMEs transition to a low-carbon 
economy with environmental and social risk management 
to be integrated into the credit decision making process. 
In addition, we are proud to report on our 2nd GHG 
emissions for FY2022 and we are considering our  
decarbonisation plan in motion.
For our customers and communities, our commitment lies 
in continuously enhancing service quality, accessibility 
and technological innovations to ensure convenience 
and seamless banking experiences. We strongly believe 
in social and financial inclusion and therefore strive to 
create equal opportunities by empowering those in need 
with a special focus on people with disabilities. We are 
also dedicated to investing back into the communities

aim to leverage the benefits of modern society and foster 
sustainable economic growth.
For our people, they are our greatest asset, and we

Population growth in Egypt poses both challenges and 
opportunities for the banking sector, as the country 
faces problems associated with poverty, inequality, water 
scarcity, air pollution, and climate change. The Egyptian 
banking sector is taking concrete steps to address these 
challenges by developing sustainable finance strategies 
focused on social and environmental risk management, 
responsible lending practices, and green financing, 
following the related guiding principles published by the 
Central Bank of Egypt (CBE).
Climate change  
Considering Egypt’s high vulnerability to climate change, 
adapting to the adverse impacts of climate change 
is imperative as part of the efforts to mitigate climate 
change.
Adaptation to climate change and disaster risk reduction 
was the primary objectives of Egypt’s first National 
Strategy in 2011. A comprehensive national climate 
change strategy until 2050 has also been requested by 
the Egyptian National Climate Change Council (NCCC) to 
address the impacts of climate change.
Some of Egypt’s strategic goals in this front include 
sustainable economic growth in key economic sectors 
with low emissions, resilient and adaptive response to

Sustainable finance  
The term sustainable finance may be referred to as 
financial tools designed to address challenges related to 
climate change, as well as other social and environmental 
issues. This funding is raised from the public as well as 
private sectors including institutional investors, banks, 
financial regulators, central banks, and international finance 
institutions. Sustainable financing can be availed in the 
form of inclusive loans and subsidies, guarantees and 
risk insurance, international climate finance, green bonds, 
sovereign wealth funds, state-owned enterprises, and 
more.   
In September 2020, the Egyptian government introduced 
its Green Financing Framework and successfully launched 
its inaugural USD750 million Green Bond, this marked the 
first sovereign Green Bond in the Middle East and North 
Africa.
Egypt has actively utilized sustainable financing tools to 
support its development initiatives. In 2014, the IBRD 
provided a $300 million line of credit to MSMEDA, while 
the EBRD issued a $30 million loan to the NBE to promote 
renewable power generation and energy efficiency. In

Regulations
The CBE has put together a set of sustainable finance 
regulations in 2021 in line with the Egypt Vision 2030 
and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). These 
regulations are based on six key principles: building the 
required knowledge and capabilities, improving sustainable 
finance, ensuring stakeholder involvement, climate change 
risk management, application of sustainable principles in 
internal operations and activities, and reporting. 
Prepared in accordance to international best practices, 
these regulations are intended to direct and guide banks 
towards financing projects that are sustainable and create 
investment opportunities for investors that are inclined

Financial inclusion
The National Financial Inclusion Strategy (2022-2025), 
has been launched recently by the CBE with an aim of 
improving financial inclusion by enhancing access to formal 
financial services for underserved populations, promoting 
financial literacy, strengthening financial infrastructure, and 
enhancing financial inclusion among women and people 
with disabilities. The CBE is collaborating with government 
agencies, financial institutions, and stakeholders to achieve 
these objectives, including establishing a financial inclusion 
fund and offering microfinance services. The strategy has 
positively impacted Egypt’s economy by expanding credit 
opportunities, encouraging innovation, and facilitating 
access to financial services.

Our approach to ESG 
Future outlook 
Egypt aims to convert half of its national projects to green 
ones by 2024 through bonds. ADCB Egypt looks forward to 
launching green products in line with ADCB Group’s Green 
Bond Framework in 2023.
ADCB Egypt is actively working to adopt, implement and 
align to all frameworks, policies, procedures, and guidelines 
issued by ADCB Group. In 2022, ADCB Group approved 
a new sustainability strategy and governance framework 
with full Board oversight and coverage across the Bank. 
The Group has also launched a Group Sustainability 
Policy and an Environmental and Social Risk Management 
(ESRM) Policy to integrate the assessment and mitigation 
of ESG risks associated with credit counterparties within 
its Enterprise Risk Management framework. These policies 
are further supported by topic-specific and sectoral policies, 
operating procedures, and guidelines to ensure effective 
implementation across the group.
ADCB Egypt’s commitment to sustainability and environmental 
responsibility is in line with ADCB Group’s vision of launching 
an integrated sustainability strategy and issuing green products.

Case study
By hosting COP27, Egypt has emerged as a key 
participant of the global sustainability dialogue, 
showcasing its accomplishments as well as 
emphasising the need for actions that are more decisive 
and ambitious. A major focus of COP27 was on Egypt’s 
challenges, including efforts to close the gender gap, 
vulnerability caused by climate changes, and the rapid 
expansion of solar energy. These challenges have not 
only shaped the way regional stakeholders analyse 
threats and concerns related to sustainability in Egypt, 
but also played a role in the development of solutions 
for ensuring compliance and maintaining leadership.   
ADCB Egypt announced the sponsorship of “Journey to 
the Climate Summit”, in an initiative to raise awareness 
of climate change, which was launched under the 
auspices of the Ministries of Planning and Economic 
Development, Youth, Sports, Environment and Military 
Production, and in cooperation with the United Nations 
Development Program and the Sustainable Services 
Project funded by the United States Agency for 
International Development (USAID), ahead of Egypt’s 
hosting of the Summit Climate COP27.
The Bank’s sponsorship for this innovative initiative 
comes in implementation of its plan to achieve

ADCB Egypt operates as a subsidiary of the ADCB Group 
and aligns with the Group’s comprehensive Environmental 
and Social Risk Management (ESRM) framework.

committees and groups, including the Group Board Risk 
Committee (BRC), the Group Risk Management Committee 
(RMC), the Group Sustainability Committee (GSC), and 
the Environmental and Social Risk Management (ESRM) 
Working Group. By adhering to the Group’s policies and 
practices, ADCB Egypt ensures a consistent approach to 
managing E&S risks across the organisation.
The Risk Management Committee (RMC) is responsible 
for endorsing the Group’s ESRM Policy, including E&S 
risk appetite prior to approval by BRC. The committee 
is responsible for approving E&S risk assessment 
methodology, models, and frameworks. The committee 
also approves E&S scenario analysis and stress testing 
results and E&S risk as part of ICAAP . The Group

or be affected by climate change and other forms of

Energy
ADCB Egypt’s energy consumption in 2022 involved 
electricity usage as the primary source of energy, diesel 
fuel to power emergency generators, natural gas for 
heating, and fuel in owned vehicles. These activities 
resulted in a total energy consumption of 10,339 GJ at 
the head office. The Bank is actively working to reduce its 
energy consumption by replacing fluorescent lamps with 
LED ones across all its branches and offices. Moreover, 
the head office has a building management system (BMS) 
installed to monitor and control indoor AC systems, 
pumps, and chillers operations. 
Water
ADCB Egypt’s branches use municipal water for drinking 
and sanitary purposes. Since these branches are located 
in residential areas, the water bills are usually consolidated 
across all building users. In 2022, the Bank installed water 
meters for some branches and is currently working on 
installing them for the remaining ones. To further reduce 
water consumption, ADCB Egypt equipped all its branches 
with water-efficient faucets and installed a wastewater 
recycling system in the head office building. The head 
office building consumed a total of 12.1 mega litres of 
municipal water in 2022.

of waste across all of its branches

Paper
Paper consumption constitutes a significant portion of the 
materials used across ADCB Egypt’s forty-nine branches. 
ADCB Egypt’s head office consumed 9.9 tons of paper in 
2022, signifying an increase from the amount consumed in 
2021. We aim to decrease our consumption with the aid 
of the Bank’s ambitious digitisation strategy, which aims to 
minimise its reliance on paper in all business operations.

A substantial amount of the Bank’s material consumption 
comes from Bank cards. In 2022, the Bank produced 
and issued 21,387 banking cards. However, the Bank 
will consider enhancing its cards’ environmental footprint 
recycling programs and exploring the use of bio-
composites as a PVC alternative.

Empowering People with Disabilities 
(PwDs)
ADCB Egypt is deeply committed to empowering 
individuals with disabilities and ensuring their full inclusion 
in the banking sector. ADCB Egypt has taken significant 
steps to provide equal opportunities and convenient 
access to its services for people with disabilities.
Braille documents
ADCB Egypt has made banking documents available 
in Braille, allowing visually impaired customers to 
independently access and understand the content 
without relying on assistance from others. This initiative 
promotes autonomy and privacy, enabling visually 
impaired individuals to manage their finances with ease 
and confidence.
Sign language
ADCB Egypt recognises the importance of effective 
communication and has specially trained its customer 
service employees in sign language. The Bank’s 
employees can effectively communicate with hearing-
impaired individuals and address their inquiries 
comprehensively by being proficient in sign language. 
This ensures that hearing-impaired customers receive the 
same level of service and support as any other customer, 
fostering an inclusive environment where everyone feels 
valued and understood.

ADCB Egypt is committed to inclusive empowerment and 
has launched the “Erada” package in 2021. Erada is the 
first package of its kind to provide integrated services with 
banking and non-banking features designed to support 
people with disabilities. This initiative is in line with the Central 
CBE directions and the nation’s goal to consider people with 
disabilities into society.
Erada package
This comprehensive package provides banking facilities 
and services to help people with disabilities (PwDs) in their 
daily lives. The package is launched without administrative 
expenses and without a minimum balance. The banking 
benefits also include the issuance of a “Meeza” prepaid 
card, and registration for all digital banking services to 
access accounts, transfer and pay from anywhere, and no 
administrative fees. 
Non-banking benefits are also offered and they include the 
issuance of medical discounts card with a wide coverage 
network around the country, discounts on various medical 
services, and compensatory devices for people with 
disabilities without any extra fees to claim the discounts.

customers, employees, and the wider community.

Corporate governance
Board nomination and evaluation
ADCB Egypt follows specific criteria for nominating 
and selecting its highest governance body, the Board 
of Directors, and its committees. These criteria include 
ensuring that board members possess diversified 
qualifications, capabilities, skills, expertise, and knowledge 
that are relevant to their positions. It is crucial for board 
members to have a comprehensive understanding of their 
responsibilities as well as the duties of the committees 
they are involved in. 
ADCB Egypt conducts a comprehensive annual evaluation 
of the Board and its committees. This evaluation assesses 
their performance, effectiveness, and adherence to 
governance principles. Board members also engage in 
self-assessment to reflect on their individual contributions. 
These rigorous evaluation processes aim to ensure a high 
level of board performance, accountability, and adherence 
to governance standards.

ethical and professional conduct for all employees and

a subsidiary. It emphasises the importance of treating

Why it matters
In today’s fast-paced world, risk management, 
cybersecurity, and data privacy have become paramount 
concerns for every organisation. ADCB Egypt fully 
acknowledges the critical importance of comprehensive 
risk oversight, effective mitigation strategies, cyberliteracy, 
and ensuring the utmost protection of customer data. As 
a result, we remain dedicated to continuously enhancing 
our technological infrastructure and implementing rigorous 
frameworks to ensure robust protection against any future 
uncertainties.
Our approach and progress
To ensure effective risk management, ADCB Egypt’s 
Risk strategy aims at full alignment with ADCB Group’s 
Risk Strategy. Continuous follow-up and revision are in 
place to reach this goal. ADCB Egypt has established 
comprehensive risk management policies and systems in 
line with this goal. These policies and systems undergo 
regular review and updates to align with market dynamics, 
product offerings, and best practices. Our risk department, 
in coordination with various operating units, plays a pivotal 
role in identifying, evaluating, and mitigating financial risks.

projects and initiatives such as T24 upgrade, convene, 
digital onboarding, IPN, Cisco call center, ITM, and more.

systems are robust and well-protected.

ADCB Egypt’s Management Executive Committee oversees the implementation of the strategy and reports to the Board of Directors.
The Group Board Executive Committee (BEC) is responsible for oversight of the group’s Sustainability Strategy,  encompassing climate-related risks and opportunities, and receives an annual update. The BEC updates 
the full Board of Directors, as required.
ADCB Group’s Board Risk Committee (BRC) ensures a robust Environmental and Social Risk Management (ESRM) culture within the Group by delegating responsibilities for  decision making and controls to appropriate 
personnel, units, and committees. BRC approves Group’s ESRM Policy, including climate-related risk appetite statements,and further delegating E&S Risk oversight and management activities as required.
Read more on our governance approach, including management’s role, under ADCB Group’s Sustainability Strategy on page 25

As per ADCB Group’s ESRM Policy, the Bank will assess the various climate-related risks and opportunities and their impact in the short, medium, and long term and takes this into consideration when developing it’s 
strategic commitments.
• Launch ADCB Egypt’s sustainable finance policy
• Adding ESG criteria to its credit assessment to incentivize sustainable economies
To support implementation of our commitments, climate-related risk appetite statements have been defined. The risk appetite statement is reviewed and approved by ADCB Group’s Board Risk Committee 
on an annual basis and monitored on a quarterly basis
ADCB Group is in the process of running the inaugural climate risk stress test (CRST) to assess the impact of different climate scenarios on customers and their resilience to transition and physical risks. The 
CRST follows a methodology leveraging the Bank’s existing models to run the scenarios and ECL to determine stressed provision levels.

The ESRM Policy establishes the process for identifying and assessing E&S risks and how it integrates into the overall enterprise risk management. This encompasses the definition of E&S risks (incl. physical and 
transition climate risks) and transmission channels (credit, market, operational, reputational), and a materiality assessment.
The process for managing climate-related risks is outlined in our process flow for E&S risk assessment and involves four key steps:
a. exclusion list screening,
b. restricted list screening,
c. for qualifying transactions an ESG scorecard assessment,
d. and where required enhanced due diligence to mitigate negative impacts
This process is supported by sector addendums to provide 1st and 2nd lines of defense with additional guidance for key high risk sectors.
Read more on our approach to risk management under Environmental and Social Risk Management on pages 43-45

CEO letter
IHAB ELSEWERKY  |  ADCB Egypt’s CEO & Managing Director 
Navigating progress with purpose
As we reflect on 2024, we take pride in the strides ADCB Egypt has 
made in strengthening financial resilience, advancing sustainability, 
and deepening our impact within the communities we serve. The 
past year has been a testament to our unwavering commitment 
to responsible growth, innovation, and inclusivity.
Our journey has been shaped by an evolving financial landscape, 
where resilience and strategic foresight have been critical in 
navigating macroeconomic challenges. We have continued to align 
with the ADCB Group’s directives and Egypt’s national priorities, 
ensuring that our business remains well-positioned to support 
economic stability while advancing a sustainable future.
Accelerating our sustainability commitments
Sustainability remains at the core of our strategy, and 2024 
marked a year of transformative progress in our ESG journey. 
We successfully developed and published our baseline financed 
emissions assessment in line with the PCAF Standard, starting 
with the construction and real estate sector—an essential step 
in refining our approach to climate risk. We also expanded our 
sustainable finance portfolio to EGP 8.5 billion, a 240% year-on-
year increase, with EGP 4.27 billion dedicated to green lending 
and EGP 4.25 billion directed toward social lending.

criteria into vendor onboarding through an ESG scoring system

Building Management System (BMS) to optimize energy use, 
while implementing a comprehensive recycling program at our 
headquarters to reinforce our environmental stewardship.
Furthering our role as a catalyst for innovation, ADCB Egypt

INTRODUCTION
Egypt’s sustainability outlook 2024 
Advancing Egypt’s sustainability agenda 
Egypt remains steadfast in its commitment to sustainability, reinforcing its position as a regional leader in ESG initiatives. 
Throughout 2024, the country continued to implement ambitious strategies and action plans that align with global sustainability 
goals, including the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the Paris Agreement. 
A key milestone in this journey was the updated Egypt Vision 2030, which provides a comprehensive roadmap for sustainable 
development. The revised vision is underpinned by four guiding principles—balanced growth, resilience and risk management, 
competitive and diversified economy, and environmental sustainability. Additionally, seven enablers have been identified as critical 
to achieving these goals, including financing, technology and innovation, digital transformation, data availability, supportive 
legislative and institutional frameworks, a strong cultural system, and population growth control. These elements collectively 
shape Egypt’s efforts to foster a more sustainable and inclusive economic landscape.

INTRODUCTION
Expanding green finance 
In the 2024 Sustainable Banking and Finance Network (SBFN) 
Global Progress Brief, Egypt moved up from "Developing-
Implementation" to "Advancing-Implementation," indicating 
the country has introduced tools and supervisory approaches 
to support the implementation of national and regional 
sustainable finance frameworks, covering multiple parts of 
the financial system. The SBFN, an initiative of the World 
Bank's International Finance Corporation (IFC), benchmarks 
sustainable finance trends and initiatives across 66 member 
countries, all emerging markets and developing economies. 
The SBFN's Progression Matrix measures progress made at 
the country level based on three main pillars: ESG Integration, 
Climate Risk Management, and Financing Sustainability.
In September 2024, the Ministry of Planning, Economic 
Development, and International Cooperation launched Egypt's 
Integrated National Financing Strategy during the UN Summit 
of the Future in Washington, DC. Developed in collaboration 
with multiple UN agencies, the strategy adopts a Financing for 
All (F2F) approach, shifting from traditional financing models 
to a comprehensive approach for sustainable development. 
It prioritizes seven sectors critical to national progress: social 
protection, sanitation, health, transportation, education, 
climate change, and women's empowerment.
Committing to financial inclusion

Committing to financial inclusion 
Financial inclusion remains a cornerstone of Egypt’s economic 
development strategy, with the CBE spearheading efforts to 
expand access to financial services. By the end of 2024, 
Egypt’s financial inclusion rate reached 74.8%, a significant 
increase from 70.7% in 2023. Approximately 52 million citizens 
now own and actively use financial accounts, encompassing 
banks, Egypt Post, mobile wallets, and prepaid cards.
The CBE’s Financial Inclusion Strategy (2020–2025) has 
been instrumental in driving this progress, with targeted 
initiatives to empower women, youth, and entrepreneurs. The 
financial inclusion rate for women reached 68.8%, reflecting 
a remarkable growth of 295% since 2016. Similarly, youth 
financial inclusion (ages 15-35) saw a 65% increase, reaching 
53.1%. Regulatory measures, such as the simplified account 
opening process using only a National ID, have further 
facilitated access to financial services. These efforts align with 
Egypt’s broader vision of fostering economic empowerment 
and social equity.

Governance and  
regulatory framework 
Egypt has made significant advancements in sustainability 
governance, ensuring that the financial and corporate sectors 
integrate ESG principles into their operations. The CBE’s 
Sustainable Finance Principles provide a comprehensive 
framework for banks to embed sustainability into their 
business models, requiring mandatory quarterly disclosures 
on the implementation of these principles, along with annual 
sustainability and carbon footprint reporting.
In parallel, the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) mandates 
ESG disclosures for companies listed on the Egyptian Stock 
Exchange and those operating in the non-banking financial 
sector, aligning with global ESG and climate reporting 
frameworks and standards. These regulations reinforce 
transparency, accountability, and responsible business 
practices across the financial landscape.
A key example of Egypt’s commitment to strengthening 
financial governance and security was the launch of the 
first edition of the “Egypt Fraud Combating Forum” in 2024, 
hosted by the CBE. This globally recognized initiative brought 
together banking and financial sector leaders to address 
emerging fraud trends and best practices for risk mitigation, 
further solidifying Egypt’s position as a leader in financial 
integrity and security.

OUR APPROACH TO ESG 
Our purpose at ADCB Egypt is to combine strong 
local roots with global standards. We work within 
Egypt’s Vision 2030 framework and support the UN’s 
Sustainable Development Goals, all while following 
ADCB Group’s proven approach to banking.
We keep our mission simple: to become the most 
trusted bank for Egyptians. This means offering 
smart, secure banking solutions and building 
genuine, long-term relationships with our customers. 
Five basic principles guide our work: we care about 
our customers, respect our commitments, maintain 
strict discipline, set ambitious goals, and conduct 
business with complete integrity.
As an established Egyptian bank, we take our 
leadership role seriously. Our daily operations reflect 
this responsibility through clear reporting and strict 
adherence to the Central Bank of Egypt’s guidelines 
for sustainable finance.
We turn these principles into practical actions. Each 
year, we publish detailed ESG reports to share our 
progress. We create financial products that support 
environmental protection, use ADCB Group’s tested 
standards for green bonds, and make sustainable 
choices across our business operations.

Trust through sound governance
Our governance structure guides how we make decisions, 
manage risk, and put our values into practice. We’ve designed 
clear processes to ensure accountability at every level and 
help us make sound decisions that earn the trust of our 
stakeholders.
Board leadership
Our Board of Directors provides oversight for the Bank’s 
operations with a special focus on sustainability. The Board 
sets ESG goals aligned with our Group’s purpose, identifies 
environmental and social risks, monitors progress against 
sustainability targets, and reviews environmental and social 
risk policies.
Sustainability Committee
Meeting quarterly, our Sustainability Committee evaluates 
sustainable banking performance, reviews proposed
