recommendations to the Board. This committee includes 
leaders from various bank departments, connecting 
sustainability goals with daily operations.

Refining our Focus on Material Topics
In 2024, ADCB Egypt enhanced its materiality assessment 
by adopting a double materiality approach, building on 
the impact-focused assessments conducted in previous 
years. The Bank integrated the frameworks of both the GRI 
and the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards to guide 
the process. 
This reassessment reflected evolving stakeholder 
expectations, recent initiatives across the Bank, and 
continued alignment with ADCB Group’s strategic direction. 
Through a combination of comprehensive desktop research, 
peer benchmarking, and targeted stakeholder engagement, 
we were able to refine and reprioritise the most relevant 
sustainability topics to our business. 
This ensures that our ESG strategy and action plan 
remain responsive, focused, and aligned with both market 
expectations and long-term impact.

guided by global frameworks such as the GRI Standards and the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards, as well as industry-
specific considerations from SASB and other ESG rating agencies. This was further refined to reflect Egypt’s national priorities, 
local regulatory developments, and the Bank’s evolving business strategy.

emissions across all activities, and second, to incorporate all carbon-intensive sectors within the lending portfolio.

Sustainable finance
Why it matters
Sustainable finance is essential to driving long-term value creation, benefiting both our business and the broader economy. By 
integrating ESG considerations into our investments, lending, products, and services, ADCB Egypt enhances business resilience, 
generates financial returns, and supports customers in their transition to more sustainable practices. Promoting sustainable 
finance also strengthens our role in advancing environmental and socioeconomic progress, aligning with national and global 
sustainability directives. Through this approach, ADCB Egypt contributes to the transformation of the financial sector while 
minimizing the environmental impact associated with our portfolio.
Our approach and progress
ADCB Egypt is dedicated to integrating sustainability into its financial practices, aligning with global and national sustainability 
goals. The Bank has expanded its support for low-carbon services and environmental projects, ensuring that environmental 
and social risk management (ESRM) is embedded in its operations and lending portfolio.
ADCB Egypt has significantly expanded both its green and social finance portfolios, reaching EGP 4.272 billion in green finance 
and EGP 4.247 billion in social finance as of December 2024. It has also introduced new sustainable financial products to 
support clients’ transitions to more sustainable operations.

Financing Egypt’s leading circular leather complex
As part of its sustainable finance strategy, ADCB Egypt 
financed the Leather and More Industrial Complex in Robbiki 
Leather City. Spanning 210,000 m², the facility is the largest 
of its kind in Africa and the Middle East. It features three 
integrated projects: a leather tanning and finishing plant, a 
recycling facility converting leather waste into organic solid 
and liquid fertilizers and amino acids, and a gelatin and 
chemicals production unit.
The project adopts a circular economy model, transforming 
waste into valuable products and minimizing environmental 
harm. By using advanced, environmentally friendly 
technologies, it supports the local production of organic 
nitrogen fertilizers, reduces reliance on imports, and boosts 
the export of finished leather. Located within a fully equipped 
industrial zone, the complex benefits from access to key 
infrastructure including water, wastewater, electricity, and 
natural gas networks.
The project is expected to create more than 1,000 jobs 
and contribute significantly to reducing industrial waste. An 
environmental risk assessment was conducted to ensure 
full alignment with Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency 
regulations and sustainability best practices.

ADCB Egypt remains committed to advancing its sustainable finance agenda by expanding its green finance initiatives and 
integrating ESG considerations into its operations. In 2024, the Bank exceeded its sustainable finance target, achieving

Bank will further develop its Green Facility Program, a tailored financial solution for corporate and SME clients, aimed at 
supporting energy efficiency, renewable energy, and water-efficient technologies. To enhance transparency and efficiency,

the integration of sustainable finance KPIs for corporate clients. This will enable the Bank to offer more targeted financial 
products that drive environmental and social impact.
Additionally, the Bank will continue strengthening its Environmental and Social Risk Management (ESRM) framework by 
supporting Credit Risk Management in materiality assessments, identifying high-risk sectors, and providing strategic

Driving climate innovation through entrepreneurship
As part of its commitment to sustainability and innovation, 
ADCB Egypt sponsored “ClimaTech Accelerator 2024”, the 
country’s first dedicated climate technology accelerator, 
launched in collaboration with NilePreneur, an initiative by 
Nile University supported by the Central Bank of Egypt. This 
initiative aligns with ADCB Egypt’s sustainability strategy 
by fostering innovative solutions to climate challenges 
and strengthening entrepreneurial ecosystems that drive 
sustainable economic growth.
The program aims to raise awareness about climate change 
and clean technologies while empowering local startups to 
develop scalable ClimaTech solutions. Through a 7-8 month 
cycle of intensive mentorship, business development, expert 
support, and networking, startups refine their business 
models, gain access to funding opportunities, and drive 
impact in areas such as sustainable agriculture, smart 
mobility, energy and water management, circular economy, 
and green construction.
In 2024, 10 startups participated in the program. One notably 
secured funding after advancing through Egypt’s Shark Tank, 
showcasing the accelerator’s role in nurturing high-potential 
climate ventures. Startups were selected based on their 
climate-tech focus, operational maturity, and scalability.

Environmental & social 
risk management
Why it matters
Environmental and social risk management (ESRM) is a 
fundamental part of our ESG risk framework and responsible 
banking approach. These risks can impact our business at 
every level, influencing our operations, financing activities, 
and long-term sustainability goals. By integrating E&S 
considerations into our risk management framework 
and lending practices, we strengthen our due diligence 
processes, mitigate potential negative impacts, and unlock 
new opportunities for sustainable growth. This proactive 
approach ensures compliance with regulations, enhances 
partnerships with socially responsible investors, and enables 
us to contribute positively to the communities we serve while 
maintaining a responsible and resilient financial institution.
Our approach and progress
ADCB Egypt is committed to strengthening its ESRM 
framework by continuously enhancing policies and standard 
operating procedures, training employees, and engaging with 
stakeholders. The Bank regularly updates its ESRM policy to 
align with evolving regulatory requirements and industry best 
practices. Through targeted training programs and workshops, 
ADCB Egypt equips its teams with the knowledge and tools 
needed to assess and manage ESG risks effectively.
To ensure ESG integration across its credit processes, the 
Bank has embedded ESG considerations into its lending

Borrowers’ ESG performance is tracked, and key indicators

Recognizing the importance of capacity building, ADCB

considerations remain a core component of its risk

analysis, the Bank enhances responsible lending practices, 
mitigates potential risks, and fosters long-term value for

E&S risk governance framework and ESRM Policy
ADCB Egypt is aligning its ESRM framework with the CBE’s regulations as well as the ADCB Group’s policies and governance 
structure, ensuring a structured approach to integrating E&S considerations into its operations and lending activities. The Bank 
has established a dedicated ESRM Working Group comprising senior management, which convenes periodically to oversee 
the implementation of E&S risk management within the credit process and address key challenges. In line with the Group’s 
ESRM Policy, ADCB Egypt is enhancing its processes by incorporating material E&S risks into its risk framework, refining due 
diligence procedures, and progressively integrating transition and physical risk assessments.

Sector-Based E&S Risk Management Progress
As ADCB Egypt continues to strengthen its Environmental and Social Risk Management (ESRM) framework, we have taken 
significant steps to enhance our understanding of E&S risks across different sectors. To support this, we have initiated a 
structured assessment of transition risk exposure and are actively working on refining our ESRM processes and procedures.
A key component of this effort is our materiality assessment, which helps identify and evaluate E&S risks relevant to our portfolio. 
This assessment provides insight into sector-specific exposures and informs our approach to risk mitigation. Currently, we 
are enhancing our methodology by integrating E&S risk assessments into our credit evaluation process and expanding our 
understanding of physical risk and overall portfolio exposure.
As part of this evolution, we are reviewing and enhancing our ESRM framework to ensure a more comprehensive and proactive 
approach to risk identification. This includes developing sector-specific risk considerations, strengthening due diligence practices, 
and preparing for future climate risk scenario testing. Our goal is to establish a robust foundation that aligns with industry best 
practices while addressing Egypt’s evolving regulatory and sustainability landscape.

E&S risk assessment process
ADCB Egypt’s E&S risk assessment at the counterparty 
level begins with an initial screening by front-line business 
units. This process includes checking against ADCB Egypt’s 
exclusions and restricted lists, followed by evaluating 
the potential E&S risk exposure of customers using a 
structured scorecard.
The scorecard incorporates both qualitative and quantitative 
factors, generating a consolidated risk rating for each customer. 
This assessment is conducted during the onboarding process 
for new clients and as part of the periodic credit review for 
existing ones.
ADCB Egypt is committed to strengthening its ESRM 
framework as it continues integrating sustainability 
considerations into its operations. The Bank aims to 
enhance climate risk assessment in lending decisions 
by embedding transition and physical risk evaluations 
into its credit processes. 
A key priority will be conducting sector-specific risk 
assessments for industries that are particularly vulnerable 
to climate change, ensuring a more informed approach 
to risk mitigation. 
The Bank will also focus on reviewing and enhancing its 
ESRM framework, refining due diligence processes and 
sector-specific evaluation methodologies. Furthermore, 
ADCB Egypt is preparing for climate stress testing under 
moderate and severe scenarios to assess the potential 
financial and operational impacts of climate change.

Operations  
and supply chain
Why it matters
Sustainable operations and a responsible supply chain are 
fundamental to reducing environmental impact, enhancing 
efficiency, and ensuring long-term business resilience. By 
integrating sustainability into energy use, waste management, 
procurement, and resource consumption, ADCB Egypt 
strengthens its operational performance while contributing 
to broader environmental and social goals. A responsible 
supply chain extends this commitment beyond the Bank’s 
direct operations, fostering ethical business practices and 
driving positive change across industries.
Our approach and progress
ADCB Egypt continues to embed sustainability into its 
operations, prioritize energy efficiency, emissions reduction, 
and responsible resource management. Investments in green 
building standards, such as EDGE certification, reflect the 
Bank’s dedication to reducing its environmental footprint. 
Waste reduction and recycling initiatives support a circular 
approach, while digital transformation helps optimize 
material consumption. 
In procurement, ESG criteria are integrated into supplier 
assessments to ensure ethical sourcing and responsible 
business practices. By strengthening sustainability across 
its operations and supply chain, ADCB Egypt is enhancing 
efficiency, mitigating risks, and reinforcing its position as a 
responsible financial institution.

Methodology and boundaries
ADCB Egypt has defined its organisational boundary as the 
businesses and operations that make up the company. For the 
current reporting period, the organisational boundary includes 
two head offices in addition to 50 branches which collectively 
have a gross floor area of 67,939 m² and employ 1,791 people1. 
This year marks the fourth carbon footprint assessment for 
ADCB Egypt, covering all the Bank’s facilities in Egypt with an 
enhanced data recording system and increased coverage of 
operational activities to include purchased goods & services, 
capital goods, waste generated in operations, and employee 
commuting. As a result, the Bank has decided to restate its 
base year to 2024 instead of 2021, as it reflects the most 
accurate and recent year of emissions.
The operational boundaries of the current assessment include 
activities that lead to emissions, whether they are direct or 
indirect. These include direct GHG emissions (Scope 1), indirect 
GHG emissions from the consumption of purchased electricity 
and chilled water (Scope 2), and indirect GHG emissions from 
other activities (Scope 3). 
To calculate the carbon footprint, ADCB Egypt followed 
established protocols and standards, including The Greenhouse 
Gas Protocol Guidelines, the 2006 Intergovernmental Panel 
on Climate Change (IPCC) Guidelines for Greenhouse Gas

Energy Management
ADCB Egypt continues to advance its energy efficiency by managing electricity and chilled water use, diesel fuel for emergency generators, and natural gas for heating, while closely monitoring fuel consumption in owned vehicles. In 2024, total 
energy consumption across our facilities reached 11,251 MWh. The Bank expanded its transition to LED lighting, achieving 100 percent LED installation across all branches and offices. Additionally, five branches were equipped with energy-efficient air 
conditioning units.
At the head office, a Building Management System (BMS) automates the control of AC systems, pumps, and chillers to ensure optimal energy use. Indoor units follow preset schedules and activate automatically at assigned temperature setpoints. When the 
schedule ends, the units shut down without the need for manual input. Operators can also manage settings through a centralized workstation or local thermostats. That controls AC systems, pumps, and chillers to optimize energy efficiency.
To further reduce energy waste, the Bank integrates automated energy-saving measures across both open and closed areas. In open spaces, lighting runs on a schedule and indoor AC units follow predefined temperature settings. In closed areas, motion

As part of ADCB Egypt’s commitment to reducing its 
environmental footprint, the Bank has integrated green building 
practices into its operations. A key milestone in this journey is 
obtaining EDGE (Excellence in Design for Greater Efficiencies) 
certification, reinforcing the Bank’s focus on energy efficiency, 
water conservation, and sustainable construction materials. 
In 2024, ADCB Egypt successfully qualified 10 branches and 
its head office for EDGE certification, representing 21% of 
its total premises. These certified buildings now operate with 
enhanced energy efficiency, reduced water consumption, 
and lower embodied carbon in materials, aligning with 
global sustainability standards and the Bank’s long-term 
environmental goals. 
Beyond reducing operational impact, this initiative strengthens 
ADCB Egypt’s position as a leader in sustainable banking. 
By embedding resource efficiency into its physical footprint, 
the Bank is driving a broader shift toward green infrastructure 
within the financial sector, setting an example for responsible 
corporate practices.
Building on this momentum, ADCB Egypt aims to certify 
five additional branches in 2025, with the long-term goal 
of achieving EDGE certification across its entire network.

Driving efficiencies for customers
ADCB Egypt is continuously modernizing its banking experience, integrating digital innovations that enhance accessibility, security, and convenience. At the Electronic Area in the Head Office, 
e-brochures at ATMs provide customers with instant access to product information and banking services, ensuring seamless engagement with ADCB’s digital offerings.
Enhancing digital accessibility, ADCB Egypt has streamlined the digital onboarding process, enabling customers to open accounts quickly and effortlessly. Security and ease of use are further 
reinforced by the integration of Biometric Face ID in the mobile app, allowing customers to access their accounts seamlessly with facial recognition.
Beyond accessibility, ADCB Egypt empowers customers with greater financial control. I-Score inquiries are now available through ATMs and mobile banking, providing instant insights into credit 
status. For international transactions, Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC) automatically converts payments in real-time, simplifying cross-border purchases.
Further optimizing the Banking experience, ADCB Egypt has enhanced ATM functionalities through CX Banking software, improving transaction speed and personalization. Wallet cash-in and 
cash-out at off-site ATMs extend financial accessibility, while Mobile ATMs bring banking services directly to customers, ensuring convenience wherever they are.

ADCB Egypt’s Board of Directors serves as the highest governance body, with a responsibility for overseeing the Bank’s 
Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance. The Board is responsible for setting the ESG strategy, managing 
associated risks, monitoring performance, and ensuring transparency and accountability. To uphold strong governance

Board independence is essential for fostering objective decision-making and maintaining a governance structure that prioritizes 
transparency and accountability. In line with the Corporate Governance regulations and standards set by the CBE, ADCB Egypt

The Board is structured with a majority of non-executive members, at least two independent Board members are appointed, 
each eligible to serve for two terms with a maximum period of six consecutive or separate years. These measures reinforce a 
governance framework that minimizes conflicts of interest while promoting the Bank’s long-term strategic vision.

in early stages, foundational steps have been taken to better 
understand and address climate-related exposures. In 2024, 
ADCB Egypt published its first financed emissions report 
focusing on two key sectors as a starting point to measure 
and manage the emissions linked to its lending activities. 
This effort complements the Bank’s ongoing assessment of its 
operational GHG emissions, forming a baseline for integrating 
climate considerations into future risk assessments.
Building on its existing ESRM framework, which already 
supports the identification of environmental and social risks 
in credit decisions, the Bank aims to progressively strengthen 
its approach to climate risk. As its capacity and data maturity 
evolve, ADCB Egypt intends to explore climate scenario 
analysis and stress testing to evaluate the potential impact 
of climate risks on its portfolio under different transition and 
physical risk scenarios. This evolving approach reflects the 
Bank’s commitment to embedding climate-related financial 
risk management into its broader risk governance and

Corruption
ADCB Egypt upholds the highest standards of ethical conduct and maintains a zero-tolerance policy towards bribery and 
corruption. The bank ensures full compliance with all applicable anti-bribery and corruption laws across the markets in which 
it operates. Its policy is built on regular risk assessments and mandates that all records and financial transactions remain fair, 
accurate, and properly documented. Employees, directors, and associated persons are required to adhere to these principles 
in all business dealings.
The anti-bribery and corruption framework emphasizes transparency, reasonableness, and accountability, ensuring that all 
activities are conducted without intent to bribe or corrupt, remain proportionate to professional relationships, and are authorized 
at appropriate levels of seniority. Any form of bribery whether through direct or indirect payments, solicitation, or facilitation to 
gain an unfair business advantage is strictly prohibited. Additionally, ADCB Egypt enforces stringent oversight on third-party 
relationships, mitigating the risk of bribery or corruption by external service providers and joint ventures acting on its behalf. To 
strengthen awareness and compliance, the Bank implements mandatory training programs, including targeted sessions tailored 
to specific roles, reinforcing its commitment to ethical business practices and good corporate governance.

Scope of reporting
The KPIs included cover our activities undertaken during the 2024 fiscal year (1 January – 31 December 2024), along with 
historical data on the previous fiscal years (2021, 2022 and 2023), subject to the availability of data. The data presented in this 
section covers the operations of the two head offices and 50 branches of the Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank Egypt (referred to 
as ‘ADCB Egypt).
Restatements of prior reporting
The measurement and reporting of ESG metrics involves a degree of variability in the data due to changes in the data collection 
process and calculation methodologies. We have highlighted instances of restatements of prior year data 2023, as footnotes 
to the disclosures within this ‘Data and assurance’ section.
Basis of reporting for GHG metrics
Our reporting methodology for the GHG emissions reported for 2024 (1 January – 31 December 2024) along with historical data 
on the previous years 2022 and 2023, is aligned to the guidance in The Greenhouse Gas Protocol: A Corporate Accounting and 
Reporting Standard. We report GHG emissions in tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e), a universal unit of measurement 
to indicate the global warming potential (GWP) of each of the six greenhouse gases, expressed in terms of the GWP of one 
unit of carbon dioxide.

Progress
ADCB Egypt’s Management Executive Committee oversees the implementation of the strategy. The Management Executive Committee (MEC) is responsible for oversight of the Sustainability 
Strategy, encompassing climate-related risks and opportunities, and receives an annual update. The BEC updates the full Board of Directors, as required.
ADCB Egypt’s Board Risk Committee (BRC) ensures a robust Environmental and Social Risk Management (ESRM) culture within the Group by delegating responsibilities for decision making 
and controls to appropriate personnel, units, and committees. BRC approves Group’s ESRM Policy, including climate-related risk appetite statements, and further delegating E&S Risk 
oversight and management activities as required.

Progress
As per ADCB Group’s ESRM Policy, the Bank will assess the various climate-related risks and opportunities and their impact in the short, medium, and long term and takes this into 
consideration when developing its strategic commitments. In 2024, the Bank has:
• Launched ADCB Egypt’s Sustainable Finance Framework 
• Integrated ESG criteria to its credit assessments
To support implementation of our commitments, climate-related risk appetite statements have been defined. The risk appetite statement is reviewed and approved by ADCB Group’s Board 
Risk Committee on an annual basis and monitored on a quarterly basis ADCB Group is in the process of running the inaugural climate risk stress test (CRST) to assess the impact of different 
climate scenarios on customers and their resilience to transition and physical risks. The CRST follows a methodology leveraging the Bank’s existing models to run the scenarios and ECL 
to determine stressed provision levels.

The process for managing climate-related risks is outlined in our process flow for E&S risk assessment and involves four key steps:
a. exclusion list screening,
b. restricted list screening,
c. for qualifying transactions an ESG scorecard assessment,

Masader Environmental & Energy Services S.A.E (the ‘Assurance Provider’) has been engaged by ADCB Egypt (the ‘Reporting

the ADCB Egypt 2024 ESG Report (the ‘Report’).
Scope, Subject Matter and Limitations
The subject matter of the Report is the Reporting Organization ESG performance data and information for the year ended 
31 December 2024. The scope of assurance is limited to a review of the Selected Information listed below:
• ADCB Egypt’s ESG Management
• Stakeholder Engagement
• Materiality Assessment
The assurance process was subject to the following limitations and exclusions:
• Verifying the data or information provided by ADCB Egypt stated in the Introduction section, ADCB Egypt’s CEO Letter. 
• Appropriateness of definitions and any internal reporting criteria adopted by ADCB Egypt for its disclosures.
• Appropriateness of any new commitments and objectives established and communicated by ADCB Egypt.
• Content of external websites or documents linked from the Report and ADCB Egypt.
We have not been engaged to::
• Verify any statement indicating the intention, opinion, belief and/or aspiration of ADCB Egypt.

Navigating progress with purpose
As we reflect on 2024, we take pride in the strides ADCB Egypt has 
made in strengthening financial resilience, advancing sustainability, 
and deepening our impact within the communities we serve. The 
past year has been a testament to our unwavering commitment 
to responsible growth, innovation, and inclusivity.
Our journey has been shaped by an evolving financial landscape, 
where resilience and strategic foresight have been critical in 
navigating macroeconomic challenges. We have continued to align 
with the ADCB Group’s directives and Egypt’s national priorities, 
ensuring that our business remains well-positioned to support 
economic stability while advancing a sustainable future.
Accelerating our sustainability commitments
Sustainability remains at the core of our strategy, and 2024 
marked a year of transformative progress in our ESG journey. 
We successfully developed and published our baseline financed 
emissions assessment in line with the PCAF Standard, starting 
with the construction and real estate sector—an essential step 
in refining our approach to climate risk. We also expanded our 
sustainable finance portfolio to EGP 8.5 billion, a 240% year-on-
year increase, with EGP 4.27 billion dedicated to green lending 
and EGP 4.25 billion directed toward social lending.

INTRODUCTION
Egypt’s sustainability outlook 2024 
Advancing Egypt’s sustainability agenda 
Egypt remains steadfast in its commitment to sustainability, reinforcing its position as a regional leader in ESG initiatives. 
Throughout 2024, the country continued to implement ambitious strategies and action plans that align with global sustainability 
goals, including the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the Paris Agreement. 
A key milestone in this journey was the updated Egypt Vision 2030, which provides a comprehensive roadmap for sustainable 
development. The revised vision is underpinned by four guiding principles—balanced growth, resilience and risk management, 
competitive and diversified economy, and environmental sustainability. Additionally, seven enablers have been identified as critical 
to achieving these goals, including financing, technology and innovation, digital transformation, data availability, supportive 
legislative and institutional frameworks, a strong cultural system, and population growth control. These elements collectively 
shape Egypt’s efforts to foster a more sustainable and inclusive economic landscape.
Environmental stewardship and climate commitments 
As climate change presents mounting global challenges, Egypt has reinforced its commitment to climate action through 
comprehensive policies and strategic frameworks. The country has updated its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) to

promotes circular economy practices and pollution control. In 2024, the government enhanced transparency by publishing online

in environmental governance.

INTRODUCTION
Expanding green finance 
In the 2024 Sustainable Banking and Finance Network (SBFN) 
Global Progress Brief, Egypt moved up from "Developing-
Implementation" to "Advancing-Implementation," indicating 
the country has introduced tools and supervisory approaches 
to support the implementation of national and regional 
sustainable finance frameworks, covering multiple parts of 
the financial system. The SBFN, an initiative of the World 
Bank's International Finance Corporation (IFC), benchmarks 
sustainable finance trends and initiatives across 66 member 
countries, all emerging markets and developing economies. 
The SBFN's Progression Matrix measures progress made at 
the country level based on three main pillars: ESG Integration, 
Climate Risk Management, and Financing Sustainability.
In September 2024, the Ministry of Planning, Economic 
Development, and International Cooperation launched Egypt's 
Integrated National Financing Strategy during the UN Summit 
of the Future in Washington, DC. Developed in collaboration 
with multiple UN agencies, the strategy adopts a Financing for 
All (F2F) approach, shifting from traditional financing models 
to a comprehensive approach for sustainable development. 
It prioritizes seven sectors critical to national progress: social 
protection, sanitation, health, transportation, education, 
climate change, and women's empowerment.

Committing to financial inclusion 
Financial inclusion remains a cornerstone of Egypt’s economic 
development strategy, with the CBE spearheading efforts to 
expand access to financial services. By the end of 2024, 
Egypt’s financial inclusion rate reached 74.8%, a significant 
increase from 70.7% in 2023. Approximately 52 million citizens 
now own and actively use financial accounts, encompassing 
banks, Egypt Post, mobile wallets, and prepaid cards.
The CBE’s Financial Inclusion Strategy (2020–2025) has 
been instrumental in driving this progress, with targeted 
initiatives to empower women, youth, and entrepreneurs. The 
financial inclusion rate for women reached 68.8%, reflecting 
a remarkable growth of 295% since 2016. Similarly, youth 
financial inclusion (ages 15-35) saw a 65% increase, reaching 
53.1%. Regulatory measures, such as the simplified account 
opening process using only a National ID, have further 
facilitated access to financial services. These efforts align with 
Egypt’s broader vision of fostering economic empowerment 
and social equity.

Egypt has made significant advancements in sustainability 
governance, ensuring that the financial and corporate sectors 
integrate ESG principles into their operations. The CBE’s 
Sustainable Finance Principles provide a comprehensive 
framework for banks to embed sustainability into their 
business models, requiring mandatory quarterly disclosures 
on the implementation of these principles, along with annual 
sustainability and carbon footprint reporting.
In parallel, the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) mandates 
ESG disclosures for companies listed on the Egyptian Stock 
Exchange and those operating in the non-banking financial 
sector, aligning with global ESG and climate reporting 
frameworks and standards. These regulations reinforce 
transparency, accountability, and responsible business 
practices across the financial landscape.
A key example of Egypt’s commitment to strengthening

business with complete integrity.

choices across our business operations.

Refining our Focus on Material Topics
In 2024, ADCB Egypt enhanced its materiality assessment 
by adopting a double materiality approach, building on 
the impact-focused assessments conducted in previous 
years. The Bank integrated the frameworks of both the GRI 
and the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards to guide 
the process. 
This reassessment reflected evolving stakeholder 
expectations, recent initiatives across the Bank, and 
continued alignment with ADCB Group’s strategic direction. 
Through a combination of comprehensive desktop research, 
peer benchmarking, and targeted stakeholder engagement, 
we were able to refine and reprioritise the most relevant 
sustainability topics to our business. 
This ensures that our ESG strategy and action plan 
remain responsive, focused, and aligned with both market 
expectations and long-term impact.

ADCB Egypt began by reviewing a broad set of sustainability topics across environmental, social, and governance dimensions, 
guided by global frameworks such as the GRI Standards and the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards, as well as industry-
specific considerations from SASB and other ESG rating agencies. This was further refined to reflect Egypt’s national priorities, 
local regulatory developments, and the Bank’s evolving business strategy.

means the Bank supports responsible 
development and upholds high standards in 
its lending portfolio.

financing a project with unchecked climate 
or human rights risks could lead to pollution, 
community opposition, or other negative 
outcomes.

left behind (a “digital divide”), and over-
reliance on technology without safeguards 
might result in data privacy issues or system 
outages affecting customers. Additionally, 
insufficient innovation could make our 
services outdated, indirectly slowing financial 
sector development.

compliance strengthen stakeholder confidence 
in the Banking sector. By adhering to high 
ethical standards, transparency, and regulatory

integrity and fair business practices. This 
contributes to market stability and economic 
resilience in Egypt – a well-governed bank is 
less likely to suffer crises that could impact 
the wider economy. 
Poor governance or lapses in compliance can 
lead to misconduct, financial irregularities, 
or corruption. This not only harms the Bank 
(through scandals or failures) but can also 
undermine trust in financial institutions 
broadly, potentially destabilizing markets 
and hurting investors and customers. For 
example, a governance failure could result 
in losses for depositors or shareholders, 
affecting livelihoods and confidence in the 
Banking system.

A strong anti-financial crime program 
(covering anti-money laundering, anti-bribery, 
counter-terrorism financing, etc.) helps 
protect the integrity of the financial system 
and the broader economy. By preventing illicit 
finance, ADCB Egypt supports government 
anti-corruption efforts and promotes an 
ethical business environment. This has 
societal benefits: reducing corruption and 
money laundering channels contributes to 
economic fairness and security in Egypt. 
If the Bank’s defences against financial crime 
are weak, it could inadvertently facilitate 
corruption, fraud, or terrorist financing. 
Such illicit activities, when undetected, can 
funnel resources to criminal enterprises or 
extremists, undermining law and order and 
economic stability. Moreover, association with 
any financial crime scandal would severely 
damage trust in the Bank and could have 
industry-wide repercussions if confidence in 
banks’ ability to combat crime falters.

Managing financed

Why it matters
A significant portion of ADCB Egypt’s greenhouse gas (GHG) 
emissions stems from its financing and investment activities, 
categorized as Scope 3 financed emissions under the 
GHG Protocol.
In alignment with ADCB Group, ADCB Egypt has begun 
assessing its financed emissions to identify high-emission 
sectors, manage climate-related risks and opportunities, 
and support Egypt’s climate strategy. This assessment will 
also guide portfolio alignment and the development of client 
transition plans.
Our approach and progress
As part of our commitment to measuring and managing 
climate-related risks, ADCB Egypt has completed its first 
financed emissions assessment and published its inaugural 
Financed Emissions Report. This milestone reflects our 
dedication to transparency, as we disclose emissions data 
in line with the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials 
(PCAF) and the Global GHG Accounting and Reporting 
Standard for the Financial Industry.
ADCB Egypt has reported financed emissions for its corporate 
loans portfolio, specifically focusing on the Commercial and 
Residential Real Estate sector, using 2022 as the base year. 
The assessment covers corporate loans classified under the 
“Business Loans and Unlisted Equity” asset class, as defined 
by the PCAF Standard. Within the Real Estate sector, we have 
identified two key sub-sectors within the value chain: Building

greenhouse gases specified in the Kyoto Protocol and reporting results in metric tons of CO2 equivalent (tCO2e), with financial 
data converted from Egyptian Pounds to US Dollars using the year-end 2022 exchange rate. After detailed calculations, the 
methodology includes thorough analysis and presentation of findings along with data quality scoring compliant with PCAF

Sustainable finance
Why it matters
Sustainable finance is essential to driving long-term value creation, benefiting both our business and the broader economy. By 
integrating ESG considerations into our investments, lending, products, and services, ADCB Egypt enhances business resilience, 
generates financial returns, and supports customers in their transition to more sustainable practices. Promoting sustainable 
finance also strengthens our role in advancing environmental and socioeconomic progress, aligning with national and global 
sustainability directives. Through this approach, ADCB Egypt contributes to the transformation of the financial sector while 
minimizing the environmental impact associated with our portfolio.
Our approach and progress
ADCB Egypt is dedicated to integrating sustainability into its financial practices, aligning with global and national sustainability 
goals. The Bank has expanded its support for low-carbon services and environmental projects, ensuring that environmental 
and social risk management (ESRM) is embedded in its operations and lending portfolio.
ADCB Egypt has significantly expanded both its green and social finance portfolios, reaching EGP 4.272 billion in green finance 
and EGP 4.247 billion in social finance as of December 2024. It has also introduced new sustainable financial products to 
support clients’ transitions to more sustainable operations.

Financing Egypt’s leading circular leather complex
As part of its sustainable finance strategy, ADCB Egypt 
financed the Leather and More Industrial Complex in Robbiki 
Leather City. Spanning 210,000 m², the facility is the largest 
of its kind in Africa and the Middle East. It features three 
integrated projects: a leather tanning and finishing plant, a 
recycling facility converting leather waste into organic solid 
and liquid fertilizers and amino acids, and a gelatin and 
chemicals production unit.
The project adopts a circular economy model, transforming 
waste into valuable products and minimizing environmental 
harm. By using advanced, environmentally friendly 
technologies, it supports the local production of organic 
nitrogen fertilizers, reduces reliance on imports, and boosts 
the export of finished leather. Located within a fully equipped 
industrial zone, the complex benefits from access to key 
infrastructure including water, wastewater, electricity, and 
natural gas networks.
The project is expected to create more than 1,000 jobs 
and contribute significantly to reducing industrial waste. An 
environmental risk assessment was conducted to ensure 
full alignment with Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency 
regulations and sustainability best practices.

Portfolio exposure across diverse sectors
E&S risk assessment process
ADCB Egypt’s E&S risk assessment at the counterparty 
level begins with an initial screening by front-line business 
units. This process includes checking against ADCB Egypt’s 
exclusions and restricted lists, followed by evaluating 
the potential E&S risk exposure of customers using a 
structured scorecard.
The scorecard incorporates both qualitative and quantitative 
factors, generating a consolidated risk rating for each customer. 
This assessment is conducted during the onboarding process 
for new clients and as part of the periodic credit review for 
existing ones.
ADCB Egypt is committed to strengthening its ESRM 
framework as it continues integrating sustainability 
considerations into its operations. The Bank aims to 
enhance climate risk assessment in lending decisions 
by embedding transition and physical risk evaluations 
into its credit processes. 
A key priority will be conducting sector-specific risk 
assessments for industries that are particularly vulnerable 
to climate change, ensuring a more informed approach 
to risk mitigation. 
The Bank will also focus on reviewing and enhancing its 
ESRM framework, refining due diligence processes and 
sector-specific evaluation methodologies. Furthermore, 
ADCB Egypt is preparing for climate stress testing under 
moderate and severe scenarios to assess the potential 
financial and operational impacts of climate change.

Operations  
and supply chain
Why it matters
Sustainable operations and a responsible supply chain are 
fundamental to reducing environmental impact, enhancing 
efficiency, and ensuring long-term business resilience. By 
integrating sustainability into energy use, waste management, 
procurement, and resource consumption, ADCB Egypt 
strengthens its operational performance while contributing 
to broader environmental and social goals. A responsible 
supply chain extends this commitment beyond the Bank’s 
direct operations, fostering ethical business practices and 
driving positive change across industries.
Our approach and progress
ADCB Egypt continues to embed sustainability into its 
operations, prioritize energy efficiency, emissions reduction, 
and responsible resource management. Investments in green 
building standards, such as EDGE certification, reflect the 
Bank’s dedication to reducing its environmental footprint. 
Waste reduction and recycling initiatives support a circular 
approach, while digital transformation helps optimize 
material consumption. 
In procurement, ESG criteria are integrated into supplier 
assessments to ensure ethical sourcing and responsible 
business practices. By strengthening sustainability across 
its operations and supply chain, ADCB Egypt is enhancing 
efficiency, mitigating risks, and reinforcing its position as a 
responsible financial institution.

Methodology and boundaries
ADCB Egypt has defined its organisational boundary as the 
businesses and operations that make up the company. For the 
current reporting period, the organisational boundary includes 
two head offices in addition to 50 branches which collectively 
have a gross floor area of 67,939 m² and employ 1,791 people1. 
This year marks the fourth carbon footprint assessment for 
ADCB Egypt, covering all the Bank’s facilities in Egypt with an 
enhanced data recording system and increased coverage of 
operational activities to include purchased goods & services, 
capital goods, waste generated in operations, and employee 
commuting. As a result, the Bank has decided to restate its 
base year to 2024 instead of 2021, as it reflects the most 
accurate and recent year of emissions.
The operational boundaries of the current assessment include 
activities that lead to emissions, whether they are direct or 
indirect. These include direct GHG emissions (Scope 1), indirect 
GHG emissions from the consumption of purchased electricity 
and chilled water (Scope 2), and indirect GHG emissions from 
other activities (Scope 3). 
To calculate the carbon footprint, ADCB Egypt followed 
established protocols and standards, including The Greenhouse 
Gas Protocol Guidelines, the 2006 Intergovernmental Panel 
on Climate Change (IPCC) Guidelines for Greenhouse Gas

Energy Management
ADCB Egypt continues to advance its energy efficiency by managing electricity and chilled water use, diesel fuel for emergency generators, and natural gas for heating, while closely monitoring fuel consumption in owned vehicles. In 2024, total 
energy consumption across our facilities reached 11,251 MWh. The Bank expanded its transition to LED lighting, achieving 100 percent LED installation across all branches and offices. Additionally, five branches were equipped with energy-efficient air 
conditioning units.
At the head office, a Building Management System (BMS) automates the control of AC systems, pumps, and chillers to ensure optimal energy use. Indoor units follow preset schedules and activate automatically at assigned temperature setpoints. When the 
schedule ends, the units shut down without the need for manual input. Operators can also manage settings through a centralized workstation or local thermostats. That controls AC systems, pumps, and chillers to optimize energy efficiency.
To further reduce energy waste, the Bank integrates automated energy-saving measures across both open and closed areas. In open spaces, lighting runs on a schedule and indoor AC units follow predefined temperature settings. In closed areas, motion

Case Study
Advancing green building standards with EDGE certification
As part of ADCB Egypt’s commitment to reducing its 
environmental footprint, the Bank has integrated green building 
practices into its operations. A key milestone in this journey is 
obtaining EDGE (Excellence in Design for Greater Efficiencies) 
certification, reinforcing the Bank’s focus on energy efficiency, 
water conservation, and sustainable construction materials. 
In 2024, ADCB Egypt successfully qualified 10 branches and 
its head office for EDGE certification, representing 21% of 
its total premises. These certified buildings now operate with 
enhanced energy efficiency, reduced water consumption, 
and lower embodied carbon in materials, aligning with 
global sustainability standards and the Bank’s long-term 
environmental goals. 
Beyond reducing operational impact, this initiative strengthens 
ADCB Egypt’s position as a leader in sustainable banking. 
By embedding resource efficiency into its physical footprint, 
the Bank is driving a broader shift toward green infrastructure 
within the financial sector, setting an example for responsible 
corporate practices.
Building on this momentum, ADCB Egypt aims to certify 
five additional branches in 2025, with the long-term goal 
of achieving EDGE certification across its entire network.

the Bank remains committed to fostering a greener, more

Waste and recycling
ADCB Egypt is committed to minimizing the environmental 
impact of its operations by optimizing waste management 
practices. Our waste streams include general office waste, 
shredded paper, and electronic waste, which are either 
reused when possible or sold for material recovery. We 
are advancing our corporate-wide waste management 
process by standardizing waste segregation, storage, 
and disposal practices. In 2024, we established plans to 
partner with a specialized waste management company to 
implement recycling and waste handling at our Head Office, 
which accounts for nearly half of our total workforce. This 
partnership will be activated in 2025, and we plan to extend 
these practices to our branches, ensuring consistent and 
responsible waste management across our operations.
Reducing material consumption remains a key priority for ADCB 
Egypt, with a strong focus on minimizing paper usage across 
our operations. As part of our digital transformation strategy, 
we are actively working to cut down on printed materials by 
promoting digital banking, automating internal processes, and 
shifting to paperless workflows. The total waste generated 
across all ADCB Egypt facilities for the year 2024 has been 
estimated at 344 tons, based on a developed estimation 
methodology. The methodology estimates waste generation at 
ADCB Egypt facilities by applying an average waste generation

Advancing a Circular Approach
As part of our ongoing efforts to create a more sustainable and resource-efficient operation, ADCB Egypt 
has partnered with a waste management company to recycle waste generated from our head office. This 
initiative marks a significant step toward integrating circular economy principles into our waste management 
strategy, ensuring that valuable resources are repurposed rather than discarded. By embedding sustainability 
deeper into our operations, we continue to drive positive environmental impact while aligning with national 
and global sustainability goals.

Local partnerships
ADCB Egypt prioritizes local procurement as a key driver of 
sustainable economic growth and supply chain resilience. 
By sourcing locally, the Bank minimizes its carbon footprint 
while supporting national industries and businesses. 
In 2024, 96% of suppliers were local, accounting for 90% 
of total procurement spending, reinforcing the Bank’s 
commitment to strengthening the local economy.
Suppliers ESG assessment
ADCB Egypt maintains a structured approach to supply chain management under its Group-wide Procurement Policy, incorporating 
ESG criteria to evaluate and mitigate risks. The Bank requires suppliers to adhere to local laws, regulations, and the Vendor 
Code of Conduct, which outlines standards on ethics, environmental responsibility, human rights, and workplace safety.
To enhance ESG accountability, ADCB Egypt has updated its vendor onboarding process to include ESG-specific criteria, 
ensuring that new suppliers meet sustainability expectations. Additionally, an ESG scoring system has been introduced in 2024, 
applied to 11 new vendors representing 15% of our suppliers to be screened against the ESG criteria and granting a 5% bonus 
on total evaluation for suppliers demonstrating strong ESG performance.

their background or financial status, have access to essential banking services. By integrating underserved communities including 
women, youth, people with disabilities (PwDs), and small business owners into the formal financial system, ADCB Egypt helps 
create opportunities for economic empowerment and long-term financial stability. Providing tailored financial solutions and 
educational resources not only enhances financial literacy but also enables individuals to make informed financial decisions, 
fostering resilience and reducing economic disparity. Through its commitment to financial inclusion, ADCB Egypt contributes 
to national economic development and supports the broader vision of inclusive and equitable growth.

ADCB Egypt adopts a multi-faceted approach to financial inclusion by developing customized products, forming strategic 
partnerships, and delivering educational initiatives that enhance financial accessibility. 
The Bank continuously innovates to meet the evolving needs of unbanked and underserved segments, ensuring financial services 
are both inclusive and impactful.

ADCB Egypt’s Hayah package
ADCB Egypt continues to support and uplift women through 
various financial inclusion initiatives, including the Hayah 
Package. This initiative was launched to provide Egyptian 
women with financial and non-financial benefits, supporting 
their financial independence and well-being. As part of this 
initiative, ADCB Egypt successfully onboarded 1,400 women 
onto Hayah Package.

free savings account opening with no minimum balance 
requirement, free debit card issuance, and complimentary 
subscription to ADCB’s digital banking services.

a medical card that covers various healthcare and insurance 
services, offering discounts of up to 70% at medical centers, 
laboratories, and hospitals. The package also includes 
cancer insurance coverage of EGP 40,000, personal accident 
coverage of EGP 50,000, and accidental sickness coverage 
of EGP 3,000

October, offering Hayah Package customers a free voucher for 
early breast cancer diagnosis. This initiative underscores the

healthcare support, ensuring women have access to essential

Supporting youth
Go Package for youth
ADCB Egypt launched the GO Package for Youth, offering tailored benefits to make banking more accessible and rewarding. 
Through this initiative, the Bank successfully acquired 370 new-to-bank (NTB) youth from Lotus University, in addition 100 NTB 
youth from Mountain View Technical School and from GUC University.
The GO Package provides young customers with seamless banking experience, including free account opening, no monthly 
maintenance fees, and free debit card issuance. It also offers eligibility for all types of credit cards with a limit of up to EGP 
150,000.  
Additionally, customers of the GO Package receive priority consideration for summer internships at the Bank, allowing them 
to gain valuable professional experience. With an emphasis on digital convenience, the GO Package enables youth to manage 
their accounts effortlessly through online and mobile banking solutions.

Tomouh Package

Egyptian startups, this initiative aims to provide financial 
and non-financial solutions that empower entrepreneurs and 
help their businesses thrive. Through this program, the Bank 
successfully boarded 300 startup owners onto the Tomouh

hospitals, laboratories, and medical centers.

50,000, accident insurance coverage of EGP 50,000, and 
accidental medical emergency coverage of EGP 3,000.

Board Independence
Board independence is essential for fostering objective decision-making and maintaining a governance structure that prioritizes 
transparency and accountability. In line with the Corporate Governance regulations and standards set by the CBE, ADCB Egypt 
ensures that the roles of Chairperson and CEO remain separate to uphold clear lines of authority and oversight. 
The Board is structured with a majority of non-executive members, at least two independent Board members are appointed, 
each eligible to serve for two terms with a maximum period of six consecutive or separate years. These measures reinforce a 
governance framework that minimizes conflicts of interest while promoting the Bank’s long-term strategic vision.
Board nomination and evaluation
ADCB Egypt follows a structured and merit-based process when nominating Board members and forming its committees. This 
ensures that the Board comprises professionals with diverse expertise, industry knowledge, and governance capabilities. Board 
members are expected to have a thorough understanding of their roles, responsibilities, and the strategic objectives of the Bank.
To uphold strong governance practices, ADCB Egypt conducts an annual evaluation of the Board and its committees, assessing 
their performance, effectiveness, and adherence to governance principles. Board members also participate in self-assessments

ADCB Egypt acknowledges that climate change poses 
emerging risks that can manifest across various financial risk 
categories, including credit, market, and operational risks. 
While the Bank’s climate risk management practices are still 
in early stages, foundational steps have been taken to better 
understand and address climate-related exposures. In 2024, 
ADCB Egypt published its first financed emissions report 
focusing on two key sectors as a starting point to measure 
and manage the emissions linked to its lending activities. 
This effort complements the Bank’s ongoing assessment of its 
operational GHG emissions, forming a baseline for integrating 
climate considerations into future risk assessments.
Building on its existing ESRM framework, which already 
supports the identification of environmental and social risks 
in credit decisions, the Bank aims to progressively strengthen 
its approach to climate risk. As its capacity and data maturity 
evolve, ADCB Egypt intends to explore climate scenario 
analysis and stress testing to evaluate the potential impact 
of climate risks on its portfolio under different transition and 
physical risk scenarios. This evolving approach reflects the 
Bank’s commitment to embedding climate-related financial 
risk management into its broader risk governance and 
decision-making processes.

Corruption
ADCB Egypt upholds the highest standards of ethical conduct and maintains a zero-tolerance policy towards bribery and 
corruption. The bank ensures full compliance with all applicable anti-bribery and corruption laws across the markets in which 
it operates. Its policy is built on regular risk assessments and mandates that all records and financial transactions remain fair, 
accurate, and properly documented. Employees, directors, and associated persons are required to adhere to these principles 
in all business dealings.
The anti-bribery and corruption framework emphasizes transparency, reasonableness, and accountability, ensuring that all 
activities are conducted without intent to bribe or corrupt, remain proportionate to professional relationships, and are authorized 
at appropriate levels of seniority. Any form of bribery whether through direct or indirect payments, solicitation, or facilitation to 
gain an unfair business advantage is strictly prohibited. Additionally, ADCB Egypt enforces stringent oversight on third-party 
relationships, mitigating the risk of bribery or corruption by external service providers and joint ventures acting on its behalf. To 
strengthen awareness and compliance, the Bank implements mandatory training programs, including targeted sessions tailored 
to specific roles, reinforcing its commitment to ethical business practices and good corporate governance.

to indicate the global warming potential (GWP) of each of the six greenhouse gases, expressed in terms of the GWP of one

Progress
ADCB Egypt’s Management Executive Committee oversees the implementation of the strategy. The Management Executive Committee (MEC) is responsible for oversight of the Sustainability 
Strategy, encompassing climate-related risks and opportunities, and receives an annual update. The BEC updates the full Board of Directors, as required.
ADCB Egypt’s Board Risk Committee (BRC) ensures a robust Environmental and Social Risk Management (ESRM) culture within the Group by delegating responsibilities for decision making 
and controls to appropriate personnel, units, and committees. BRC approves Group’s ESRM Policy, including climate-related risk appetite statements, and further delegating E&S Risk 
oversight and management activities as required.

Progress
As per ADCB Group’s ESRM Policy, the Bank will assess the various climate-related risks and opportunities and their impact in the short, medium, and long term and takes this into 
consideration when developing its strategic commitments. In 2024, the Bank has:
• Launched ADCB Egypt’s Sustainable Finance Framework 
• Integrated ESG criteria to its credit assessments
To support implementation of our commitments, climate-related risk appetite statements have been defined. The risk appetite statement is reviewed and approved by ADCB Group’s Board 
Risk Committee on an annual basis and monitored on a quarterly basis ADCB Group is in the process of running the inaugural climate risk stress test (CRST) to assess the impact of different 
climate scenarios on customers and their resilience to transition and physical risks. The CRST follows a methodology leveraging the Bank’s existing models to run the scenarios and ECL 
to determine stressed provision levels.

Introduction and Objectives of the Engagement
Masader Environmental & Energy Services S.A.E (the ‘Assurance Provider’) has been engaged by ADCB Egypt (the ‘Reporting 
Organization’) to provide Moderate Assurance Type 1 (the ‘Assurance’) regarding adherence to the AA1000AS v3 (2020) over 
the ADCB Egypt 2024 ESG Report (the ‘Report’).
Scope, Subject Matter and Limitations
The subject matter of the Report is the Reporting Organization ESG performance data and information for the year ended 
31 December 2024. The scope of assurance is limited to a review of the Selected Information listed below:
• ADCB Egypt’s ESG Management
• Stakeholder Engagement
• Materiality Assessment
The assurance process was subject to the following limitations and exclusions:
• Verifying the data or information provided by ADCB Egypt stated in the Introduction section, ADCB Egypt’s CEO Letter. 
• Appropriateness of definitions and any internal reporting criteria adopted by ADCB Egypt for its disclosures.
• Appropriateness of any new commitments and objectives established and communicated by ADCB Egypt.
• Content of external websites or documents linked from the Report and ADCB Egypt.
We have not been engaged to::
• Verify any statement indicating the intention, opinion, belief and/or aspiration of ADCB Egypt.
• Determining which, if any, recommendations should be implemented.

ينتمى بنك أبوظبي التجاري مصر إلي مجموعة أبوظبي التجاري والتى تُعد ثالث أكبر مؤسسة مالية في دولة الإمارات العربية المتحدة. وتم إطلاق علامة بنك أبوظبي التجاري في مصر عام 2020 بعد الاستحواذ على مجموعة بنك الإتحاد الوطنى على مستوى العالم.
ويعمل بنك ابوظبي التجاري مصر على تقديم حلول مصرفية مبتكرة وقيادة طفرة التحول الرقمى وذلك بهدف ان يصبح البنك الأكثر تفضيلاً لعملائه وبدعم من المجموعة في الامارات. ويقوم البنك بخدمة شرائح العملاء المختلفة سواء في مجال التجزئة المصرفية وكبار العملاء والشركات الكبرى بالإضافة إلى قطاع الشركات الصغيرة والمتوسطة من خلال تقديم مجموعة متكاملة من المنتجات والخدمات المصرفية على أعلى مستوى. ويتيح البنك لعملائه من الشركات والافراد قنوات رقمية متطورة فضلاً عن شبكة الفروع وأجهزة الصراف الآلي المنتشرة حول الجمهورية.
ويحرص بنك أبوظبى التجارى مصر على خدمة الاقتصاد الوطني بما يتماشى مع رؤية مصر 2030، كما يشارك في تمويل عدد من المشاريع القومية البارزة، كما يتبنى البنك رؤية متكاملة لدعم مبدأ “الدمج عبر التمكين” لدمج الأشخاص ذوي الهمم في النظام المصرفي وتقديم منتجات وخدمات مصممةً خصيصاً لتلبية احتياجاتهم.
واستطاع بنك أبوظبي التجاري مصر التميز في السوق المصرفى المصري منذ انطلاقته وتحقيق عدد من الانجازات في وقت قياسي توجت بحصوله على العديد من الجوائز المرموقة لريادته فى التحول الرقمي ومبادراته لدمج الأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة وبرنامج تأهيل وتوظيف شباب الخريجين.

banking in Egypt, covering the period from June 2024 to June 2025. In 
this report, Arab African International Bank is referred to as “AAIB”, “the 
Bank”, or “we”.

ABOUT 
AAIB
Arab African 
International Bank (AAIB) is a financial group that leverages
the region’s wealth in the Egyptian market. The Bank was established by 
special legislation as a joint venture between the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) 
and Kuwait Investment Authority, in which each party holds a 49.37% stake. 
AAIB has 
evolved into a fully fledged regional banking institution with an 
extensive portfolio of innovative products and services covering Retail 
Banking, Corporate and Institutional Banking, Investment Banking and 
Structured Finance (IBSF), SMEs Banking, transaction banking solutions, 
brokerage services, asset management, private equity, leasing, mortgage 
financing, micro-enterprise solutions, and sustainable finance.
AAIB promotes responsible and sustainable growth by embedding green finance 
and socially responsible investment practices across its operations. The bank actively 
supports renewable energy projects and environmentally conscious business 
ventures. Through a focus on innovation and economic resilience, AAIB continues to 
play a leading role in advancing regional development and sustainability within 
Egypt’s financial sector.
The Bank is inspired and guided by a set of values that shape our 
mindset and behavior to meet the needs of the various stakeholders.

Arab African International Bank’s (AAIB’s) corporate 
strategy identifies sustainability as a strategic priority. 
The Bank has aligned its strategy with the United 
Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the 
Paris Climate Agreement, Egypt Vision 2030, the 
Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), and the 
Central Bank of Egypt’s (CBE’s) Sustainable Financing 
Guiding Principles. In the United Arab Emirates, we are 
working on aligning our strategy with UAE Green 2015-
2030, UAE Vision 2021, UAE’s NDC and National Climate 
Change Plan 2050.
Since 2003, AAIB has integrated sustainability into its 
financial operations, with a balanced focus on social and 
environmental performance. The Bank’s sustainability 
strategy is structured around three core pillars:
-
Environmental and Social (E&S) Strategic Alignment:
AAIB ensures that its oper
ations align with global E&S
standards, supports climate change targets, and fosters
inclusive stakeholder collaboration.
-
E&S Integration: The Bank has established robust E&S
risk management structur
es, implemented enforcement
mechanisms, and maintained transparent sustainability
reporting practices.
•
Sustainable Finance: AAIB promotes green and climate
investments, measures sustainability performance, and
encourages sustainable business practices among its
clients and partners.

Arab African International Bank (AAIB) is a distinguished financial group established under special legislation as a joint venture 
between the CBE and the Kuwait Investment Authority. Each party holds a 49.37% stake in the Bank.
AAIB is present in three countries, operating a comprehensive network of branches and ATMs to serve its clients:
• Egypt: The Bank has  96  branches, strategically located across the country, including Greater Cairo (57 branches), the Delta and
Alexandria (21 branches), the Red Sea and Suez Canal region (11 branches), and Upper Egypt (7 branches). As of December 2024, the Bank
managed 543 ATMs and served a substantial client base of 595,392 customers with the support of 3,089 employees.
• UAE: AAIB operates two branches in the UAE, located in Dubai and Abu Dhabi. The Bank managed 3 ATMs, and served 4,090 clients, 
supported by a dedicated team of 85 employees.
• Lebanon: The Bank maintains one branch in Lebanon staffed by six employees.

innovative solutions and tailored support integrates sustain ability into their financial strategies and decisions.
2. Providing Diverse Range of Products: Provide a diverse range of fully-fledged products designed to meet the evolving
sustainable finance needs of AAIB clients.
3. Empowering Sustainability through Strategic Collaboration: Support clients to smoothly weave sustainability in their
strategic financial planning.

Impact Analysis and Target Setting
Context and Rationale 
The contextual focus of our impact assessment is Egypt, where the head ofice, most of the banking operations, and the consumer lending portfolio 
are based. We took a structured approach to the Bank’s portfolio impact evaluation by accounting for country-speciic sustainability-related priorities. 
The country-speciic needs 
assessment was conigured using the context module of the built-in portfolio impact assessment tool; we also relied on 
the strategic direction underlined in Egypt’s National Climate Change Strategy (NCCS) 2050, Egypt Vision 2030, and the recent Voluntary National 
Review (VNR 2021). Egypt’s most signiicant sustainability needs relate to health and safety, availability, accessibility, and quality of resources and 
services, livelihood, equality and justice, infrastructure, socioeconomic convergence, climate stability, biodiversity and healthy ecosystems, and 
circularity. The UAE’s sustainability needs do not differ greatly f
rom those of Egypt, except for the prioritization of a healthy economy and personal 
integrity and security.

Current Performance: Climate Stability
This year, the Bank measured the inanced emissions for the  iron and st eel sector as  a pilot exercise in Egypt. Financed emissions 
are calculated by the guidance provided by the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF). Speciically, we follow the Global 
GHG Accounting and Reporting Standard – Part A f or Financed Emissions, whic h outlines the leading meth odology for how inancial 
institutions should account for their Scope 3, Category 15 emissions (Investments). The analysis showed that the carbon-intensive sector 
represented 58% of the bank’s total portfolio, excluding retail loans (which were not included in this assessment). The carbon-intensive 
sector share is determined based on its proportion of the bank’s outstanding loan portfolio. The sectors classiied as carbon-intensive are 
selected in alignment with both PCAF guidelines and the IPCC sectoral deinitions. The iron and steel sector accounts for 19% of the total 
loans allocated to carbon-intensive sectors.
This sector also represents 19% of the corporate banking portfolio in Egypt and 11% of the total assessed portfolio (i.e., the total bank 
loans excluding retail loans, across both carbon-intensive and non-carbon-intensive sectors) The inanced emissions assessment 
covered 100% of the iron and steel sector, based on data quality score 4

Ethics, and the UAE Consumer Protection Procedures Manual. These policies guide the Bank’s interactions with clients and uphold 
standards of transparency, integrity, and regulatory compliance across all operations.

line employees from the branch network participated in a training program titled Customer Rights. The course covered principles of 
fairness, justice in client interactions, and proper complaint-handling procedures. The training is based on operational needs and focuses 
on staff directly interacting with clients.
AAIB also prioritizes staff training in the UAE to ensure consistent service quality and adherence to regulatory standards. Employees 
participated in the following programs:

E&S Assessment Process
The E&S assessment process is initiated by the Relationship Manager during the onboarding of a prospective borrower or the renewal of an 
existing facility. The process begins with a preliminary screening using a standardized Initial E&S Risk Screening Form, which is designed 
to Identify whether the borrower’s activity appears on the AAIB Exclusion List and determine the need for further E&S assessment based 
on borrower segmentation, facility size, and tenor.
This initial screening is reviewed by the E&S team to conirm exclusion list compliance and to assess whether the facility requires a more 
in-depth E&S assessment. If further analysis is warranted, an independent assessment—E&S Due Diligence (ESDD)—is conducted by an 
external consultant, an E, S & Climate Risk Oficer, or the Bank’s Investigation Team.
The indings of the ESDD are integrated into the borrower’s credit assessment and include review of the relevant legal documentation. 
The assessment ensures:
• Alignment of the borrower’s operations and practices with internationally recognized standards, including the IFC Performance
Standards, Equator Principles, and GRI standards.
• Proper E&S risk categorization in accordance with AAIB’s E&S Policy.
• Evaluation of borrower compliance with national regulations and legislation.

resilience, innovation, and leadership. For six decades, 
the bank has continuously evolved, demonstrating 
agility and foresight in a dynamic financial environment. 
In 2024, we reinforced our position as one of 
Egypt’s leading financial institutions through strong 
performance, a deepened commitment to sustainable 
finance, and an unwavering focus on service excellence.
Strong Performance and Sustainable Growth
AAIB’s strong financial performance in 2024 reflects 
the disciplined execution of our strategic priorities, 
prudent risk management, and adaptability amid a 
challenging macroeconomic climate. Despite currency 
devaluation, inflationary pressures, and geopolitical 
volatility, we maintained growth and preserved balance 
sheet strength.
Our liabilities-driven approach, centered on balance 
sheet optimization, risk-adjusted growth, and market 
insight, delivered clear results. T otal assets exceeded 
USD 18.2 billion, supported by a 36% increase in 
customer deposits, which reinforced liquidity and 
enabled credit expansion.
We achieved a net profit of USD 301 million, driven by 
robust core banking revenues. Net Interest Income 
reached USD 580 million and Net Banking Income USD 
702 million, reflecting nominal growth of 14.7% and 
18.4%, respectively. We maintained strong provisioning

success and market leadership.

Sustainable 
Finance
At AAIB, sustainability is not 
a mandate; it’s a mindset.
It is a commitment to 
innovation, accountability,
and inclusive growth that 
shapes a resilient future.
AAIB’s Sustainable Finance department (SF) leads 
the bank’s commitment to responsible banking and 
long-term value creation. Acting as a bridge between 
finance and environmental stewardship, the SF 
department ensures alignment with both the Central 
Bank of Egypt’s sustainability mandates and global 
frameworks such as the UN Sustainable Development 
Goals.
As the custodian of AAIB’s sustainability agenda, 
it drives adherence to key global commitments, 
including the UN Principles for Responsible Banking, 
the Equator Principles, and the UN Global Compact. 
It integrates Environmental, Social, and Governance 
(ESG) considerations across operations, fosters 
responsible finance practices, and guides business 
lines in ESG implementation and reporting.
In 2024, AAIB published a GRI-aligned sustainability 
report, and disclosed its environmental and social 
portfolio, carbon footprint, and performance 
under the Equator Principles and UN Principles for 
Responsible Banking (PRB). In addition, SF actively 
contributed to the sustainable bond issuance.
T o strengthen internal capacity, 14 targeted training 
sessions and workshops were delivered, reaching 
approximately 250 employees across various 
departments. Highlights included IFC Climate Finance

strong, with a non-performing loan ratio of just 2.8%, 
well below the 5.4% UAE average.
The branches facilitated over USD 500 million in trade 
discounting and advanced its green finance agenda 
through participation in a syndicated facility for one of 
the largest banks in Turkey. It also began upgrading its 
core banking system to launch AAIB Connect, a unified 
digital platform enhancing cross-border services and 
automation.

As AAIB continues to evolve, Risk Management 
remains at the core of safeguarding its ambitions, 
ensuring disciplined growth, institutional resilience, and 
confidence in an increasingly complex environment. 
Through a robust governance structure, enhanced 
infrastructure, and an embedded culture of 
accountability, the bank can anticipate, absorb, and 
adapt to risk with precision and foresight.
Governance and Oversight
AAIB’s risk oversight structure integrates Board and 
management-level committees, including the Board 
Risk Committee (BRC), Enterprise Risk and Control 
Committee (ERCC), and the Board Audit Committee 
(BAC), with support from ALCO and the Management 
Credit Committee. The bank’s three lines of defense 
model ensures clarity of roles across business units, 
risk and compliance functions, and internal audit. 
All controls are designed and tested in line with 
COSO principles, reinforcing AAIB’s commitment to 
transparency and operational integrity.
Credit Risk Management
AAIB has implemented detailed risk appetite 
statements across key lines of business, supported 
by robust policies and qualitative and quantitative 
client assessments. Regular stress testing informs 
strategy and sector cap adjustments, while dedicated 
frameworks proactively manage at-risk exposures. 
These efforts ensure credit growth is well-aligned with 
risk tolerance and long-term returns.

B. Classification of financial assets and financial 
liabilities
At initial recognition, financial assets are classified 
and measured according to amortized cost, fair value 
through other comprehensive income (FVTOCI) and 
fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL). 
The financial assets are classified according to how 
they are managed (the Bank’s business model) and 
their contractual cash flow characteristics.
B/1 Financial assets are measured at amortized cost if 
the following two conditions are met:
• The management intended to maintain the asset to 
collect contractual cashflows and.
• This contractual condition of financial assets will 
build cashflows on certain dates which are Solely 
Payments of Principal and Interest (SPPI).
B/2 Debt instruments have been measured at fair 
value through other comprehensive income “FVTOCI” 
if it is not measured at fair value through profit or loss 
and the following two conditions are met:
• The management intended to maintain the assets 
to collect contractual cash flow and/or sale of the 
financial assets.
B/3 Financial assets are measured at fair value 
through profit and loss “FVTPL ” if the following 
condition is met:
• The management intended to maintain the asset 
within a business model that do not aim neither 
to hold the asset nor to collect its contractual 
cashflows.
Upon initial recognition of equity investments that are 
not held for trading, the bank may choose irrevocably

Business model assessment
• The bank assesses the objective of a business model 
in which a financial asset is held at the portfolio 
level because this reflects the best way the business 
is managed, and information is presented to 
management. The information considered includes:
• The stated policies and objectives for the portfolio 
and the operation of those policies in practice, 
specially to know whether these management 
policies concentrate to gain the contractual interest 
or reconcile financial assets with financial liabilities 
which finances these assets or target cash flow 
from selling the assets.
• How the performance of the portfolio is evaluated 
and reported to the Bank’s management.
• The risks affecting the performance of the business 
model, and the financial assets held within that 
business model and how these risks are managed.
• The frequency, volume and timing of sales in 
prior periods, the reasons for such sales and their 
expectations about future sales activity. Moreover, 
the bank doesn’t focus only on information related 
to sales activity separately, but also takes into 
consideration an overall assessment on how
